(p-244) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Surat Muhammad

It is Surat al-Qital (the Chapter of Fighting), and it is Surat Muhammad (ﷺ).

His Exalted saying: ﴿Those who disbelieve and bar (others) from the way of Allah, He will render their deeds fruitless.﴾ ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds and believe in what has been sent down to Muhammad, and it is the truth from their Lord, He will remove from them their misdeeds and set right their condition.﴾ ﴿That is because those who disbelieve follow falsehood, and those who believe follow the truth from their Lord. Thus Allah sets forth for mankind their parables.﴾

His Exalted saying in this noble verse: "and bar (others) from the way of Allah." Some said: it is from ṣudūd (ṣudūd, meaning "turning away"), because ṣadda in the verse is intransitive (lāzima).

Others said: it is from ṣadd (ṣadd, meaning "barring"), because ṣadda in the verse is transitive (muta'addiya).

On this view, the object is omitted, meaning: they barred others from the way of Allah, that is, from entering Islam.

This last view is the correct one, because on the view that ṣadda is intransitive, the phrase would be a repetition of His saying "disbelieve," since disbelief is the greatest form of turning away from the way of Allah.

As for the view that ṣadda is transitive, there is no repetition, because the meaning is that they are astray themselves and lead others astray by barring them from the way of Allah. We have already mentioned, in Surat an-Nahl, in discussing His saying: ﴿We will surely give them a good life, and We will surely reward them their best of what they used to do﴾ [an-Nahl: 97], that when a word is ambiguous between emphasis (ta'kīd) and establishing new information (ta'sīs), it must be understood as establishing new information, unless there is evidence requiring otherwise.

His Exalted saying in this noble verse: "He will render their deeds fruitless" (aḍalla a'mālahum), meaning: He will nullify their reward. Whatever good a disbeliever did in this world, such as hospitality to guests, kindness to parents, protecting the neighbor, maintaining family ties, and relieving the distressed, will be nullified on the Day of Resurrection, will vanish, and will have no effect, as He said: (p-245) ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make it scattered dust.﴾ [al-Furqan: 23]. This is the correct meaning of the verse.

It has also been said: "He rendered their deeds fruitless" means He nullified their plot, which they intended to use against the Prophet (ﷺ).

His Exalted saying in this noble verse: "Those who believe and do righteous deeds and believe in what has been sent down to Muhammad, and it is the truth from their Lord, He will remove from them their misdeeds" means: He will forgive them their sins and overlook their evil deeds. "And set right their condition" means: He will set right their affairs and state with a rectification that has no corruption in it. What the Exalted One mentioned here at the beginning of this noble surah, that He nullifies the deeds of the disbelievers and preserves the deeds of the believers, has been clarified in many verses,

• such as His saying: ﴿Whoever desires the worldly life and its adornment, We will pay them in full for their deeds therein, and they will not be deprived therein.﴾ ﴿Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter but the Fire, and what they did therein will be voided, and what they used to do is worthless.﴾ [Hud: 15-16] (as it stands in the text).

• And His saying: ﴿Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, We will increase him in his harvest; and whoever desires the harvest of this world, We will give him from it, but he will have no share in the Hereafter.﴾ [ash-Shura: 20].

• And His saying: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make it scattered dust.﴾ ﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day will be better in their resting place and finer in their resort.﴾ [al-Furqan: 23-24].

We have already presented the verses clarifying this, along with some sound hadiths about it, with important further clarification in Surat Bani Isra'il, in discussing His saying: ﴿And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it with the striving due to it while he is a believer, those are the ones whose striving is appreciated﴾ [al-Isra': 19]. And in Surat an-Nahl, in discussing His saying: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, male or female, while being a believer﴾ (verse) [an-Nahl: 97]. We also mentioned a portion of it in Surat al-Ahqaf, in discussing His saying: ﴿You have used up your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them﴾ (verse) [al-Ahqaf: 20].

His Exalted saying in this noble verse: "He will render their deeds fruitless" (aḍalla a'mālahum): its root is from ḍalāl (ḍalāl, meaning "loss/vanishing") in the sense of being lost and perishing, not from ḍāllah (ḍāllah, meaning "lost camel" or the "lost one") as al-Zamakhshari claimed. It is like His saying: ﴿And what they used to invent has vanished from them﴾ [al-An'am: 24].

We have already presented the meanings of ḍalāl in the Qur'an and in the Arabic language in Surat ash-Shu'ara', in discussing His saying: ﴿He said: I did it then, and I was among the astray﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 20]. And at the end of al-Kahf, in discussing His saying: ﴿Those whose effort is lost in the life of this world﴾ (verse) [al-Kahf: 104], and in other places.

His Exalted saying in this noble verse: "Those who believe and do righteous deeds" we have already clarified at the beginning of Surat al-Kahf, in discussing His saying: ﴿And to give good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds﴾ (verse) [al-Kahf: 2]. And in Surat an-Nahl, in discussing His saying: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, male or female, while being a believer﴾ (verse) [an-Nahl: 97].

His Exalted saying in this noble verse: "and believe in what has been sent down to Muhammad" [Muhammad: 2].

Ibn Kathir said about it: it is a specific conjunction (ʿaṭf khāṣṣ) over a general one, and it is evidence that belief in him (ﷺ) after his mission is a condition for the validity of faith. End of quote from him.

His saying supports this: ﴿And whoever among the factions disbelieves in it, the Fire is his promised place. So do not be in doubt about it; indeed, it is the truth from your Lord, but most people do not believe.﴾ [Hud: 17].

His Exalted saying in this noble verse: "and it is the truth" is a parenthetical clause (jumla i'tiraḍiyya) that contains the testimony of Allah that this Qur'an, sent down upon this noble Prophet (ﷺ), is the truth from Allah, as He said: ﴿Your people denied it, while it is the truth﴾ [al-An'am: 66]. He said: ﴿And indeed it is a regret upon the disbelievers, and indeed it is the certain truth﴾ [al-Haqqah: 50-51]. And He said: ﴿Say: O mankind, the truth has come to you from your Lord, so whoever is guided, is guided only for his own soul﴾ (verse) [Yunus: 108]. And He said: ﴿O mankind, the Messenger has come to you with the truth from your Lord﴾ (verse) [an-Nisa': 170]. The verses with this meaning are many and well known.

His Exalted saying: ﴿That is because those who disbelieve follow falsehood, and those who believe follow the truth from their Lord﴾ [Muhammad: 3] means: that mentioned, namely the nullifying of the deeds of the disbelievers, that is, their being voided and perishing, and the preservation of the reward of the believers' deeds, the expiation of their misdeeds, and the rectification of their condition, all occurs because the disbelievers followed falsehood, and whoever follows falsehood, his deed is falsehood.

The Arabs call what is perishing and vanishing "bāṭil" (falsehood), and its opposite is "ḥaqq" (truth).

And because those who believe followed the truth, and the one who follows the truth, his deeds are true, so they are firm and lasting, not perishing and vanishing.

(p-247) What this noble verse includes, that difference in deeds requires difference in reward, is not thought to make them equal except by an ignorant disbeliever, who deserves rebuke for it. This has been clarified in other verses,

• such as His saying: ﴿Shall We treat the Muslims like the criminals?﴾ ﴿What is wrong with you? How do you judge?﴾ [al-Qalam: 35-36].

• And His saying: ﴿Or shall We treat those who believe and do righteous deeds like the corrupters on earth? Or shall We treat the righteous like the wicked?﴾ [Sad: 28].

• And His saying: ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds, equal in their living and their dying? Evil is what they judge.﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 21].

His Exalted saying in this noble verse: "Thus Allah sets forth for mankind their parables."

Al-Zamakhshari said about it: If you say: where is the striking of parables? I say: in making following falsehood a parable for the deeds of the disbelievers, and following the truth a parable for the deeds of the believers. Or in making misguidance a parable for the disbelievers' failure, and the expiation of misdeeds a parable for the believers' success. End of quote from him.

The original meaning of "striking parables" (ḍarb al-amthāl) is intended to explain a matter by mentioning its counterpart which serves as its parable.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 47, verse 4:**

Allah's statement: ﴿So when you meet those who disbelieve [in battle], then strike [their] necks until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them, then secure their bonds, and then either [confer] favor afterwards or ransom [them] until the war lays down its burdens.﴾

His statement, "fa-darba al-riqab" (so strike the necks), is a verbal noun (masdar) standing in for its verb, and it carries the sense of the imperative verb. It is well known that the forms of the imperative in the Arabic language are four:

The first is the imperative verb itself, as in Allah's statement: ﴿Establish prayer at the decline of the sun﴾ [al-Isra: 78].

The second is the imperative noun (ism fi'l al-amr), as in Allah's statement: ﴿Upon you is [responsibility for] yourselves﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 105].

The third is the present-tense verb preceded by the imperative lam (lam al-amr), as in Allah's statement: ﴿Then let them complete their rites and fulfil their vows﴾ [al-Hajj: 29].

The fourth is the verbal noun standing in for its verb, as in Allah's statement: ﴿So strike the necks﴾, meaning "so strike their necks," and His statement: ﴿until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them﴾, meaning "you have made slaughter among them abundant."

Al-ithkhan (inflicting slaughter) is to increase the killing of the enemy until he becomes weakened and too heavy to rise.

His statement, "fa-shuddu al-wathaq" (then secure the bonds), means "then take them captive." Al-wathaq, with either a fatha or a kasra on the waw, is the name for whatever a captive is bound with, such as a shackle or the like.

What this noble verse includes of the command to kill the disbelievers until the Muslims have inflicted slaughter upon them, and then take them captive afterwards, is clarified in other places, such as Allah's statement: ﴿It is not for a prophet to have captives until he inflicts slaughter upon the land﴾ [al-Anfal: 67]. He has also commanded their killing in other verses, such as Allah's statement: ﴿Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 5], His statement: ﴿So strike [them] upon the necks and strike from them every fingertip﴾ [al-Anfal: 12], His statement: ﴿And fight the polytheists all together﴾ [al-Tawbah: 36], and His statement: ﴿So if you overcome them in war, then disperse those behind them﴾ [al-Anfal: 57].

As for His statement in this noble verse, ﴿then either [confer] favor afterwards or ransom [them]﴾, it means: either you bestow favor upon them, or you ransom them with ransom.

It is well known that when a verbal noun is used for detailing (tafsil), its governing verb must be omitted, as he said in the Khulasah (Alfiyyah of Ibn Malik):

*And the verbal noun used for detailing, like "immā mannan," its governing verb is elided wherever it is mentioned.*

From this is the statement of the poet:

*Surely I will strive, whether to repel a calamity that is feared, or to attain the aim and the hope.*

Some scholars said: this verse is abrogated (mansukhah) by the verses we mentioned before it. Among those narrated from as saying this are Ibn 'Abbas, al-Suddi, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, and Ibn Jurayj.

Ibn Jarir reported from Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) what supports this.

Abrogation of this verse is the position of Abu Hanifah (may Allah have mercy on him), for he holds that neither favor nor ransom is permissible, since the verse is abrogated in his view. Rather, the ruler, in his view, is given the choice between killing and enslavement.

It is well known that the verses of the sword revealed in Bara'ah were revealed after this surah of fighting.

Most scholars say: the verse is not abrogated, and all the verses mentioned (p. 249) are definitive (muhkamah). Thus the ruler has the choice, and he may do what he sees as beneficial for the Muslims: favor, ransom, killing, or enslavement.

They said: the Prophet (ﷺ) killed 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'it and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith as captives on the day of Badr, and he took ransom for the other captives.

He also bestowed favor upon Thumamah ibn Uthal, the chief of Banu Hanifah, who had been enslaving captives from the Arabs and others.

Al-Shawkani said in Nayl al-Awtar: "The conclusion is that it has been established regarding the category of disbelieving captives that killing, favor, ransom, and enslavement are permissible. Whoever claims that some of these matters are restricted to some disbelievers and not others is not to be accepted in that unless there is a valid proof that specifies the general statements. What is permitted stands in the place of prohibition. The statement of 'Ali, and his action, according to some who prohibit the enslavement of Arab males, is a proof, for he enslaved the males and females of Banu Najiyah and sold them, as is well known in the books of biographies and histories." End of the relevant point.

It is well known that Banu Najiyah are Arabs.

The author of this commentary (may Allah pardon and forgive him) says: Muslims have not differed on the permissibility of ownership through slavery.

It is well known that its cause is the capture of disbelievers by Muslims in jihad. Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, in His Book, expresses ownership through slavery with the most eloquent expression in emphasizing the establishment of ownership of slaves, which is "milk al-yamin" (what the right hand possesses), because what a person's right hand possesses is entirely his property and entirely under his control, as in Allah's statement: ﴿And if you fear that you will not deal justly [with orphans], then [marry] what your right hands possess﴾ [al-Nisa: 3].

And His statement: ﴿And those who guard their private parts, except from their wives or what their right hands possess, for they are not blameworthy﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 5-6], and [in the surah] ﴿Sa'ala sa'il﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 29-30].

And His statement: ﴿And [prohibited to you are] married women, except those your right hands possess, as decreed by Allah upon you﴾ [al-Nisa: 24].

And His statement: ﴿And those who seek a writing [of manumission] from among those whom your right hands possess, then write it for them﴾ [al-Nur: 33].

And His statement: ﴿...and the neighbor who is near and the neighbor who is distant, and the companion at your side, and the traveler, and those your right hands possess﴾ [al-Nisa: 36].

And His statement: ﴿Women are not lawful for you after [these], nor [is it lawful] to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty pleases you, except those your right hand possesses﴾ [al-Ahzab: 52].

And His statement: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives whom you have given their due compensation, and those your right hand possesses from what Allah has returned to you﴾ [al-Ahzab: 50].

And His statement: (p. 250) ﴿or their women, or what their right hands possess﴾ [al-Nur: 31].

And His statement: ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford to marry free believing women, then [he may marry] from what your right hands possess of your believing young women﴾ [al-Nisa: 25].

And His statement: ﴿Those who were favored would not give their provision to those whom their right hands possess, so that they would be equal therein﴾ [al-Nahl: 71].

And His statement: ﴿Do you have among what your right hands possess any partners in what We have provided you?﴾ [al-Rum: 28].

Therefore, what is meant by "milk al-yamin" in all these verses is ownership through slavery. The hadiths and verses of this kind are too numerous to be counted, and they are well known. No one denies slavery in Islam except a stubborn person, a heretic, or one who does not believe in the Book of Allah or the Sunnah of His Messenger.

We have already mentioned the wisdom of ownership through slavery and the resolution of the difficulty concerning the ownership of a Muslim slave in the surah of Bani Isra'il, in the discussion of Allah's statement: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most suitable﴾ [al-Isra: 9].

It is well known that many of the great scholars and eminent hadith masters of the Muslims were slaves, or sons of slaves.

Thus Muhammad ibn Sirin, whose father Sirin was a slave of Anas ibn Malik.

And Makhul, who was a slave of a woman from Hudhayl, and she freed him.

Such cases are too many to be counted, as is well known.

Know that what some fanatical advocates of denying slavery in Islam claim, namely that this verse of fighting indicates the negation of slavery from its root, because it obligates one of two matters with no third, namely favor or ransom only, is an invalid argument in two respects.

The first: it involves deriving from the verse a ruling on something that is not included in it and that it does not cover at all. An argument of this kind, if it is so, is invalid, as you see.

The clarification of this is that this verse, in which the ruling on captives is divided into favor and ransom, does not definitely cover anyone except the fighting men among the disbelievers, because His statement: ﴿So strike the necks﴾ and His statement: ﴿until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them﴾ are explicit in that, as you see.

Upon the inflicting of slaughter on these fighters, He arranged with the particle "fa" (then) His statement: ﴿then secure the bonds﴾.

It is thus clear that the verse does not cover women or children at all.

What further clarifies this is that the prohibition of killing the women and children of the disbelievers is established from the Prophet (ﷺ), (p. 251) and most of those in slavery across the lands of the world are only women and children.

And if the one who claims the negation of slavery from its root admitted that the verse cannot be used as evidence for anything other than the fighting men, then, by restricting the negation of slavery he claims to the men who were captured while fighting, if he restricts it to them, he cannot then assert the negation of slavery from its root, as you see.

The second respect: it is what we have already presented of the evidences for the establishment of slavery in Islam. As for His statement in this noble verse: ﴿until the war lays down its burdens﴾, meaning: when you meet the disbelievers, then strike their necks, ﴿until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them﴾ by killing, then take them captive, ﴿until the war lays down its burdens﴾, meaning until the war ends.

The most apparent of the views on the meaning of the war laying down its burdens is that it means laying down the weapons. The Arabs call weapons "wizr" (a burden), and the Arabs use "awzar" (burdens) for implements of war and what assists in it, such as horses. From this is the statement of al-A'sha:

*And I prepared for war its burdens: long spears and male horses.*

There are other well-known views on the meaning of the burdens of war, which we have left aside because this is the most apparent to us. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 47, verse 10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Have they not travelled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? Allah destroyed them, and for the disbelievers is the like of it.﴾ We have already set out its explanation in Surah Hud, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And it is not far from the wrongdoers﴾ [Hud: 83]. We referred to the verses that clarify this in Surah al-Rum, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Have they not travelled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in strength and they tilled the earth﴾ [al-Rum: 9]. We also explained it in Surat al-Zukhruf, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿So We destroyed those who were mightier than them in might﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 8], and in al-Ahqaf, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We had certainly established them in that wherein We have not established you﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 26], and in other places.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 47, verse 13:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And how many a town, which was mightier in power than your town which has expelled you, have We destroyed, and they had no helper.﴾ The verses that clarify the meaning of this verse are those referred to within this same verse, which we mentioned before it.

As for what this noble verse includes regarding the expulsion of the Prophet ﷺ from it by the disbelievers of Makkah, he explained it in other places, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies, showing them affection, while they have disbelieved in what has come to you of the truth, expelling the Messenger and yourselves﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 1], (p-253) and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And [remember] when those who disbelieved plotted against you to restrain you or kill you or expel you﴾ [al-Anfal: 30].

They did indeed expel him in fact, through the plot mentioned. He, may He be glorified and exalted, made clear that the Prophet ﷺ and his companions, who were expelled from their homes, had no sin for which they deserved expulsion except their belief in Allah, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿[They are] those who have been evicted from their homes without right, [only] because they say, "Our Lord is Allah"﴾ [al-Hajj: 40], and He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿They expel the Messenger and yourselves because you believe in Allah, your Lord﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 1], meaning: they expel the Messenger and yourselves because of your belief in your Lord.

And He, may He be exalted, said regarding their expulsion of him: ﴿Will you not fight a people who broke their oaths and determined to expel the Messenger?﴾ [at-Tawbah: 13], and other verses besides these.

The majority of the Seven Readers recited this letter (word) with a fathah-marked hamzah after the kaf, a shaddah-marked yaa with a kasrah, and a sukoon-marked nun, except Ibn Kathir.

Ibn Kathir recited it as "wakā'in" with an alif after the kaf and a kasrah-marked hamzah.

All of them, when pausing, stop on the sukoon-marked nun, as in the state of connection, except Abu 'Amr, who stops on the yaa.

We have already presented the modes of recitation of "ka'ayyin" and its meaning, and the dialects it contains, along with some Arabic evidences, in the surah of al-Hajj, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So how many a town did We destroy while it was wrongdoing﴾ [al-Hajj: 45].

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 47 (Muhammad), verse 15:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The description of the Garden which the righteous have been promised: in it are rivers of water unaltered, and rivers of milk whose taste never changes, and rivers of wine, delicious to those who drink it﴾.

The rivers of water and the rivers of wine that Allah mentioned in this verse, He described some of their attributes in other verses, such as:

• His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Rivers flow beneath them﴾ [Muhammad: 12], in many verses;

• and His saying: ﴿and water poured out﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 31];

• and His saying: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in shades and springs﴾ [al-Mursalat: 41];

• and His saying: ﴿In it is a flowing spring﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 12]. Allah has also explained, among the attributes of the wine of Paradise, that it does not intoxicate its drinker, nor does it cause him the headache, which is pain in the head, in verses of His Book, such as:

• His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They will not be affected by it with headache, nor will they be intoxicated﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 19];

• and His saying: ﴿No headache is in it, nor are they intoxicated by it﴾ [al-Saffat: 47].

We have already explained the meaning of these verses in detail in Surah al-Ma'idah, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, intoxicants, gambling, idols, and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 90], and so on.

As for His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿unaltered﴾, it means not changed in color or taste. The word *āsin* (آسن) and *ājin* (آجن) have the same meaning, and from it is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah:

*And a watering place, unwholesome (ājin), its surroundings desolate, over whose mounds the winds scatter the droppings of camels.*

And the saying of the rajaz poet:

*And a watering place in which a raven lies dead,*
*like oil in the ajun (dark stagnant water)... I gave the people to drink from it, and I drew water.*

By what we have mentioned, you know that His saying ﴿unaltered﴾ is like His saying ﴿rivers of milk whose taste never changes﴾.

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And for them therein is every kind of fruit﴾.

Allah has already explained in Surah al-Baqarah that the fruits which the people of Paradise are provided with resemble one another in excellence, beauty, and perfection, and none of them is inferior. This is in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Every time they are provided with a fruit therefrom, they will say, "This is what we were provided with before," and they will be given it in resemblance﴾ [al-Baqarah: 25].

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they will be given boiling water to drink, which will cut their intestines to pieces﴾.

We have already presented the verses clarifying this in Surah al-Hajj, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Boiling water will be poured over their heads, by which what is in their bellies and skins will be melted﴾ [al-Hajj: 19].

**Surah al-Qital (Muhammad)**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿In it are rivers of water unaltered, and rivers of milk whose taste never changes, and rivers of wine, delicious to those who drink it, and rivers of purified honey﴾. This noble verse indicates the multiplicity of rivers along with the multiplicity of their kinds.

Another verse has come whose apparent meaning gives the impression that it is a single river, and it is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and a river﴾ [al-Qamar: 54]. The plural was already made clear in Surah al-Baqarah, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven and made them seven heavens﴾ [al-Baqarah: 29], and so on.

We have made clear that His saying "and a river" means "and rivers."

(p. 255) Its clarifying verses have already been presented in Surah al-Zukhruf, in the discussion of His words: ﴿Do they await only the Hour, that it come upon them suddenly while they are unaware?﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 66].

* *

His words, exalted is He: ﴿So how will they have [their] reminder when it comes to them?﴾

The verified view, God willing, regarding the meaning of this noble verse is that on the Day of Resurrection, when the Hour comes upon the disbelievers, they will remember and believe in God and His messengers. Yet faith at that time will not benefit them, because its time has passed. So His words "dhikraahum" (their reminder) are the subject (mubtada', the topic of the sentence), and its predicate (khabar, the comment of the sentence) is "fa-anna lahum," meaning: how will their reminder and their belief in God benefit them, when the time in which faith is accepted has already passed?

The pronoun in "jaa'at-hum" (it comes to them) refers back to the Hour, which is the Resurrection.

This meaning indicated by this noble verse, namely that the disbelievers will believe on the Day of Resurrection but their belief will not benefit them, is clarified in many verses, such as His words: ﴿They will say, "We have believed in Him." But how can they reach [it] from a distant place?﴾ [Saba': 52], and His words: ﴿On that Day Hell will be brought forth; on that Day man will remember, but how will the remembrance benefit him?﴾ [at-Tariq: 23].

We have already presented the verses clarifying this in Surah al-A'raf, in the discussion of His words: ﴿Do they await except its fulfillment?﴾ up to His words: ﴿or we be returned so that we may do other than what we used to do﴾ [al-A'raf: 53].

It is thus evident that His words, ﴿So how will they have [their] reminder when it comes to them?﴾, contain an omitted genitive construction (mudaf, the noun governing a following noun in an idafa construction, here omitted), meaning: how will they have the benefit of their reminder?

"Adh-dhikra" (reminder) is a verbal noun (ism al-masdar, a noun standing in place of the verbal noun), meaning admonition that leads to faith.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 47, verse 20:

﴿فَإذا أُنْزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ مُحْكَمَةٌ وذُكِرَ فِيها القِتالُ رَأيْتَ الَّذِينَ في قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ يَنْظُرُونَ إلَيْكَ نَظَرَ المَغْشِيِّ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ المَوْتِ﴾ 

He - Exalted and Majestic is He - mentioned in this noble verse that when He sends down a clear (muhkamah) surah, meaning one whose words and meanings are perfected and whose indication is evident, with no abrogation (naskh, the cancellation of a ruling by a later revelation) in it, and in which the obligation of fighting the disbelievers is mentioned, then as a consequence, those in whose hearts is a disease, meaning doubt and hypocrisy, look at you with the gaze of one who has fainted from death. This is because they are in the state of death, since the gaze of one in that condition has its eyes rolling and his sight wandering.

(p-256) This happened to them only because of the intensity of fear of the might of the disbelievers, against whom they were commanded to fight.

Exalted and Majestic is He has explicitly stated that this is the fear mentioned in His saying: ﴿فَإذا جاءَ الخَوْفُ رَأيْتَهم يَنْظُرُونَ إلَيْكَ تَدُورُ أعْيُنُهم كالَّذِي يُغْشى عَلَيْهِ مِنَ المَوْتِ﴾ [al-Ahzab: 19] (So when fear comes, you see them looking at you, their eyes rolling like one who faints from death).

Exalted is He has also made clear that the wealthy among these hypocrites, when Allah sends down a surah containing the command to (jihad, struggle and fighting in the way of Allah), asked the Prophet ﷺ for permission to stay behind from jihad, and Allah blamed them for that. This is in His saying: ﴿وَإذا أُنْزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ أنْ آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وجاهِدُوا مَعَ رَسُولِهِ اسْتَأْذَنَكَ أُولُو الطَّوْلِ مِنهم وقالُوا ذَرْنا نَكُنْ مَعَ القاعِدِينَ﴾ ﴿رَضُوا بِأنْ يَكُونُوا مَعَ الخَوالِفِ وطُبِعَ عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ فَهم لا يَفْقَهُونَ﴾ [al-Tawbah: 86-87] (And when a surah is sent down saying: "Believe in Allah and strive with His Messenger," those of wealth among them ask your permission and say: "Leave us, that we may be with those who sit (at home)." They are content to be with those who stay behind, and their hearts are sealed, so they do not understand).

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 47, verse 24 (part 1 of 6):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Will they not then ponder over the Qur'an, or are there locks upon their hearts?﴾

The hamza in His saying "Will they not then ponder" is for denunciation (lil-inkar), and the fa' is conjunctive (ʿatifa) upon a deleted clause (jumla mahdhufa), according to the more correct of the two opinions. The estimated meaning is: "Do they turn away from the Book of Allah, so that they do not ponder the Qur'an?" As he indicated in al-Khulasa with his saying:

"And the deletion of the thing followed, which appears here, you may permit."

As for His saying, ﴿or are there locks upon their hearts?﴾, the "am" (or) in it is disjunctive (munqati'a) with the meaning of "bal" (rather). He, may He be exalted, has denounced their turning away from pondering the Qur'an with the particle of denunciation, which is the hamza, and He explained that upon their hearts are locks which do not open to good, nor to understanding the Qur'an.

What this noble verse includes of rebuke and denunciation against those who turn away from pondering the Book of Allah has come clarified in many verses, such as:

• His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Will they not then ponder over the Qur'an? Had it been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much discrepancy.﴾ [an-Nisa': 82],
• and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Have they not pondered over the word, or has there come to them that which did not come to their forefathers of old?﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 68],
• and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿A Book which We have sent down to you, blessed, that they may ponder its verses and that those of understanding may be reminded.﴾ [Sad: 29].

He, may He be majestic and exalted, has censured the one who turns away from this great Qur'an in many verses, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the verses of his Lord and then turns away from them?﴾ [al-Kahf: 57], and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the verses of his Lord and then turns away from them?﴾ [as-Sajda: 22].

(p-257) It is known that everyone who does not occupy himself with pondering the verses of this great Qur'an, that is, scanning them, understanding them, grasping their meanings and acting upon them, then he is turning away from them and not pondering them, and so he deserves the denunciation and rebuke mentioned in the verses, if Allah has given him understanding by which he is able to ponder. The Prophet ﷺ complained to his Lord of his people's abandoning this Qur'an, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And the Messenger says, "O my Lord, indeed my people have taken this Qur'an as something abandoned."﴾ [al-Furqan: 30].

These mentioned verses indicate that pondering the Qur'an, understanding it, learning it and acting upon it is something necessary for the Muslims.

The Prophet ﷺ has also explained that those who occupy themselves with that are the best of people, as it is established from him ﷺ in the Sahih, from the hadith of Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him), that he said: "The best of you is one who learns the Qur'an and teaches it." And He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿But be rabbaniyyin (people devoted to the Lord) by what you have been teaching of the Book and by what you have been studying.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 79].

So the turning away of many regions from looking into the Book of Allah, understanding it and acting upon it, and upon the established Sunna that explains it, is among the greatest and most abhorrent of evils, even if its doers think they are upon guidance.

And it is not hidden from any intelligent person that the claim of prohibiting acting upon the Book of Allah and the Sunna of His Messenger ﷺ, by sufficing with the compiled schools (al-madhahib al-mudawwana) and the absence of need to learn them both, because there exists what suffices in place of them from the schools of the Imams, is among the greatest falsehoods.

It also contradicts the Book of Allah, the Sunna of His Messenger, the consensus (ijma') of the Companions, and contradicts the sayings of the four Imams.

(p-258) So whoever commits it opposes Allah, His Messenger, and the Companions of His Messenger all together, and the Imams, may Allah have mercy on them, as you will see its clarification, Allah willing.

Issues related to this noble verse

The first issue: Know that the saying of some later usuliyyun (scholars of the principles of jurisprudence): that pondering this great Qur'an, understanding it and acting upon it is not permissible except for the mujtahidun (qualified independent jurists) specifically, and that everyone who has not reached the degree of absolute ijtihad (ijtihad al-mutlaq) with its conditions established by them, many of which conditions are not based on any evidence from the Book, the Sunna, the consensus, qiyas (analogy) that is clear, or a report from the Companions, is a statement having no basis whatsoever in any legal evidence.

Rather, the truth beyond doubt is that everyone among the Muslims who has the capacity to learn, to understand, and to grasp the meanings of the Book and the Sunna, is obligated to learn both of them and to act upon what he knows from them.

As for acting upon them while ignorant of what he acts upon from them, that is forbidden by consensus.

As for what he knows from them with sound knowledge arising from sound learning, he may act upon it, even if it is a single verse or a single hadith.

It is known that this blame and denunciation against one who ponders the Book of Allah is general for all people.

What clarifies this is that the first addressees of it, those about whom it was revealed, were the hypocrites and the disbelievers, not one of whom fulfilled the conditions of ijtihad established by the people of usul, rather none of those conditions was with them at all. Had the Qur'an been such that benefit from acting upon it and being guided by its guidance was not possible except for the mujtahidun in the technical usuli sense, Allah would not have rebuked the disbelievers, denounced them for not being guided by its guidance, nor established the proof against them by it until they attained the conditions of ijtihad established by the later usuliyyun, as you see.

It is known that among what is established in usul is that the case of the occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul) is definitively included, and so the inclusion of the disbelievers and hypocrites in the mentioned verses is definite. Had it been impossible to benefit from the guidance of the Qur'an except for the specific mujtahidun, Allah would not have denounced the disbelievers for not pondering the Book of Allah and not acting upon it.

You have known that the reality is definitely contrary to that, and it is not hidden that the conditions of ijtihad are not required except

(p-259) in what admits of ijtihad. Matters stated in sound texts of the Book and the Sunna, ijtihad in them is not permissible for anyone, so that conditions of ijtihad would be required for them; rather there is in them nothing but following. By this you know that what the author of Maraqi al-Su'ud stated, following al-Qarafi, with his saying: "Whoever is not a mujtahid, acting from him upon the meaning of a text is among what is forbidden (yuhzal)," is not correct in its absolute form in any way, because it contradicts many verses and hadiths without relying on any evidence.

It is known that it is not permissible to restrict the generalities (umumat) of the Book and the Sunna except by evidence which must be referred to.

It is also known that the generalities of the verses and hadiths indicating the urging of all people to act upon the Book of Allah and the Sunna of His Messenger are more than can be counted, such as His saying ﷺ: "I have left among you that which, if you hold fast to it, you will never go astray: the Book of Allah and my Sunna," and His saying ﷺ: "Upon you is my Sunna," the hadith, and what is similar to that which cannot be counted.

So restricting all those texts to the specific mujtahidun, and absolutely prohibiting benefit from the guidance of the Book and the Sunna to others, requires evidence from the Book of Allah or the Sunna of His Messenger ﷺ, and it is not valid to restrict those texts by the opinions of groups of later scholars who acknowledge about themselves that they are muqallidun (imitators).

It is known that the pure imitator (al-muqallid al-sirf) may not be counted among the scholars nor among the heirs of the Prophets, as you will see its clarification, Allah willing.

Said the author of Maraqi al-Su'ud in Nashr al-Bunud, in his explanation of his verse mentioned

(p-260) just above, the following text: "He means that the non-mujtahid is forbidden (yuhzal lahu), that is, he is prevented from acting upon the meaning of a text from the Book or the Sunna even if its chain is sound, because of the possibility of its accidental features (awarid) of abrogation, restriction, specification, and other accidental features which only the mujtahid can master. Nothing delivers him from Allah except the taqlid of a mujtahid," said al-Qarafi. The purpose of his words ends here, in his own wording.

By this you know that there is no basis for it, nor for al-Qarafi who followed it, in preventing all Muslims who are not mujtahids from acting upon the Book of Allah and the Sunna of His Messenger, merely because of the bare possibility of the accidental features that may affect the texts of the Book and the Sunna, such as abrogation, specification, restriction and the like. This is rejected from two aspects:

The first: the original state is freedom from abrogation until the arrival of the abrogating text is established; a general text is apparent in generality until the arrival of the specifying text is established; an absolute text is apparent in its absoluteness until the arrival of the restricting text is established; a text must be acted upon until abrogation is established by a legal evidence; and an apparent text must be acted upon, whether general, absolute or otherwise, until an evidence arrives diverting it from the apparent to the less likely possibility, as is known in its proper place.

The first to claim that it is not permissible to act upon the general text until one searches for the specifier and does not find it, and similar to that, was Abu al-Abbas ibn Surayj, and groups of later scholars followed him, until they ruled upon that a consensus by narration without any foundation.

Ibn al-Qasim al-Abbadi clarified their error in that in the Ayat al-Bayyinat, in his commentary on the place of Ibn al-Subki's statement in Jam' al-Jawami': "The general text is relied upon during the Prophet's lifetime before searching for the specifier, and likewise after his death, contrary to Ibn Surayj." End of quotation.

In any case, the apparent meanings of texts, whether of generality, absoluteness and the like, may not be abandoned except by evidence which must be referred to, of a specifier or restrictor, not merely because of the bare possibility, as is known in its proper place.

(p-261) The claim of many later scholars that it is obligatory to cease acting upon it until one searches for the specifier and restrictor, for example, is contrary to the verified position.

The second aspect: when the non-mujtahid learns the verses of the Qur'an, or some hadiths of the Prophet ﷺ, in order to act upon them, he learns that general or absolute text, and learns with it its specifier and restrictor if it is specified or restricted, and learns its abrogating text if it is abrogated. Learning that is very easy, by asking knowledgeable scholars and consulting the books of tafsir and hadith that are relied upon in that. The Companions in the first age would learn a verse and act upon it, and a hadith and act upon it, and none of them refrained from acting upon that until he attained the rank of absolute ijtihad. Often a person acts upon what he knows, so he is taught what he did not know, as His saying, may He be exalted, indicates: ﴿And fear Allah; Allah teaches you﴾ [al-Baqara: 282], and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, if you fear Allah, He will grant you a criterion (furqan)﴾ [al-Anfal: 29], according to the view that the furqan is beneficial knowledge by which truth is distinguished from falsehood.

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger; He will give you a double portion of His mercy and make for you a light by which you will walk﴾ [al-Hadid: 28], to the end of the verse.

This taqwa, by which the verses indicate that Allah teaches its possessor by means of it what he did not know, is nothing more than his acting upon what he knows of the command of Allah and what is upon him; so it is acting upon part of what he knows, and Allah increases him with knowledge of what he did not know.

Therefore, the saying that prohibits acting upon what one knows of the Book and the Sunna until one attains the rank of absolute ijtihad is itself the very effort to deprive all Muslims from benefiting from the light of the Qur'an, until they attain a condition which is absent in the belief of those who say so. And attributing such a thing to Allah, to His Book and to the Sunna of His Messenger is, as you see, [a grave matter].

(p-262) Important admonition:

Every Muslim who fears being exposed before his Lord on the Day of Resurrection must reflect upon this, so that he may see for himself the way out of this great predicament and this supreme calamity, which has spread over most of the lands of the Muslims in the inhabited world.

It is the claim of self-sufficiency from the Book of Allah and the Sunna of His Messenger, complete self-sufficiency in all rulings, of worship and transactions, punishments and other than that, by the compiled schools.

This is built upon two premises:

The first: that acting upon the Book and the Sunna is not permissible except for the mujtahidun.

The second: that the mujtahidun are entirely non-existent, with not a single one of them present in the world, and that on the basis of these two premises, acting upon the Book of Allah and the Sunna of His Messenger is absolutely prohibited for all people on earth, and one suffices with the compiled schools in their place.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 47, verse 24 (part 2 of 6):**

Many of them went further than this, prohibiting *taqlid* (blind adherence to a scholar's opinion) of any school other than the four *madhhabs* (legal schools), and holding that this prohibition must continue until the end of time.

So reflect, my brother, may Allah have mercy on you: how can any Muslim permit himself to claim that it is forbidden to be guided by the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ), and that there is no obligation to learn and act upon them, being content instead with the words of men who are not infallible and about whom there is no dispute that they err?

If their intention is that the Book and the Sunnah need not be learned, and that other sources suffice in their place, then this is a great calumny, an abominable statement and a falsehood.

If their intention is that learning them is difficult and beyond reach, then this too is a false claim, because learning the Book and the Sunnah is easier than learning the widespread and extremely complex matters of opinion (*ra'y*) and *ijtihad* (independent legal reasoning), despite their intricacy and volume. Allah, exalted is He, says repeatedly in Surah al-Qamar: ﴿And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?﴾ [Al-Qamar: 17, 22, 32, 40]. He, exalted is He, also says in Surah al-Dukhan: ﴿Indeed, We have made it easy in your tongue that they might remember﴾ [Al-Dukhan: 58], and in Surah Maryam: ﴿So We have only made it easy in your tongue that you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous and warn thereby a hostile people﴾ [Maryam: 97].

Thus it is a Book made easy by the ease of Allah for whomever Allah grants success in acting upon it. Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Rather, it is clear signs preserved in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge﴾ [Al-'Ankabut: 49], and He says: ﴿And We had certainly brought them a Book which We detailed with knowledge, as guidance and mercy for a people who believe﴾ [Al-A'raf: 52].

There is no doubt that whoever distances himself from its guidance is attempting to distance himself from the guidance and mercy of Allah.

There is also no doubt that this great Qur'an is the light which Allah sent down to His earth so that it may be used for illumination, and by its light the truth may be distinguished from falsehood, the good from the bad, the beneficial from the harmful, and right guidance from error.

Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿O mankind, there has certainly come to you a proof from your Lord, and We have sent down to you a manifest light﴾ [Al-Nisa': 174]. He, exalted is He, also says: ﴿There has certainly come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book, by which Allah guides those who pursue His pleasure to the ways of peace and brings them out of darkness into light by His permission and guides them to a straight path﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 15]. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you an inspiration of Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor [what] faith [was], but We made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants﴾ [Al-Shura: 52]. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿So believe in Allah and His Messenger and the light which We have sent down﴾ [Al-Taghabun: 8]. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿So those who believed in him, honoured him, supported him and followed the light which was sent down with him - it is those who will be the successful﴾ [Al-A'raf: 157].

So when you know, O Muslim, that this great Qur'an is the light which Allah sent down to be used for illumination and to be guided by its guidance upon His earth, how can you be content for your insight to be blinded to the light?

Do not be one whose insight is like that of a bat, and beware of being among those of whom it was said:

*Bats, whom the day blinded with its light,*
*and a piece of the darkest night agreed with them.*
*Like the day, it increases the sight of creation*
*with light, and blinds the eyes of the bat.*

﴿The lightning nearly snatches away their sight﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 20]. ﴿Is one who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind? Only the people of understanding will be reminded﴾ [Al-Ra'd: 19].

There is no doubt that whoever's insight is blinded to the light stumbles about in darkness, and ﴿whomever Allah does not give light, for him there is no light﴾ [Al-Nur: 40].

By this, O fair-minded Muslim, you know that it is obligatory upon you to strive diligently and exert yourself in learning the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ) by beneficial and productive means, and to act upon everything that Allah has taught you from them with sound knowledge.

And know that learning the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger in this age is far easier than it was in the earlier centuries, because it is easy to know everything relating to them: abrogating and abrogated texts (*naskh* and *mansukh*, the abrogating and the abrogated), general and specific (*'amm* and *khass*), absolute and restricted (*mutlaq* and *muqayyad*), summary and explained (*mujmal* and *mubayyan*), and the conditions of the transmitters of hadith, and the distinction between sound (*sahih*) and weak (*da'if*) reports. This is because all of it has been preserved, perfected and recorded, so all of it has been made easy to access today.

Every verse of the Book of Allah has been known, along with what was said about it by the Prophet (ﷺ), then by the Companions, the Successors and the great exegetes (*mufassirun*).

All the hadiths narrated from him (ﷺ) have been memorised and recorded, and the status of their texts (*matn*) and chains (*asanid*), and the defects (*'illah*) and weaknesses that may affect them, have been known.

Therefore, all the conditions which they stipulated for *ijtihad* are very easy to attain for everyone whom Allah has granted understanding and knowledge.

The abrogating and abrogated, the general and specific, the absolute and restricted, and similar matters are easy to know today for everyone who examines the Book and the Sunnah, among those whom Allah has granted understanding and enabled to learn the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger.

And know, O fair-minded Muslim, that among the most shameful falsehoods and the greatest untruths spoken against Allah, His Book, His Prophet and his pure Sunnah is what Shaykh Ahmad al-Sawi said in his commentary (*hashiyah*) on the *Tafsir al-Jalalayn*, in his remarks on Surah al-Kahf and Surah Al 'Imran. Countless people who call themselves students of knowledge have been deceived by his words, because they cannot distinguish between truth and falsehood.

Al-Sawi, the aforementioned, said in his commentary on Allah's words ﴿And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow"﴾ [Al-Kahf: 23], after mentioning the opinions concerning the separation of the exception (*istithna'*) from what it qualifies by a period of time, the following text: "Most of the four *madhhabs* are contrary to all of that, for the condition for the resolution of oaths by means of the exception (*mashi'ah*) is that it be connected, and that it be intended to resolve the oath. A pause for breath, coughing or sneezing does not harm it. It is not permissible to follow the opinion of anyone other than the four *madhhabs*, even if it agrees with the saying of the Companions, the sound hadith or the verse. Whoever departs from the four *madhhabs* is astray and misleads others, and this may lead him to disbelief, because taking the apparent meanings of the Book and the Sunnah is one of the roots of disbelief." End of quotation, verbatim.

So reflect, my brother, may Allah have mercy on you, on how shameful and false this statement is, and how audacious its author is against Allah, His Book, the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions. ﴿Glory be to You! This is a great slander﴾ [Al-Nur: 16].

As for his saying that it is not permissible to depart from the four *madhhabs* even when their opinions oppose the Book, the Sunnah and the sayings of the Companions, this is a false statement, refuted by the Book, the Sunnah, the consensus (*ijma'*) of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, and the consensus of the four Imams themselves, as we will see explained, with what is sufficient, if Allah wills, in the issues that follow this one. Whoever supports it is the astray one who misleads others.

As for his saying that taking the apparent meanings of the Book and the Sunnah is one of the roots of disbelief, this too is among the most shameful and greatest falsehoods, and whoever says it is among the greatest violators of the sanctity of the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ). ﴿Glory be to You! This is a great slander﴾.

The indisputable verification, which was the position of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the majority of the scholars of the Muslims, is that it is not permissible under any circumstances, in any way, to depart from the apparent meaning of the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) unless there exists a sound, legally valid proof that diverts from the apparent meaning to a less probable possibility.

The claim that acting upon the apparent meanings of the Book and the Sunnah is one of the roots of disbelief never comes from a scholar of the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger. It comes only from one who has no knowledge of the Book and the Sunnah at all, for out of ignorance of them he believes their apparent meaning to be disbelief. In reality, their apparent meaning is further from what he supposes than the sun is from the touch.

What makes this clear to you is that this verse of al-Kahf, which al-Sawi thought means that the apparent meaning resolves oaths by a conditional exception whose timing comes after the oath, and that this contradicts the four *madhhabs*, and on this basis he built the claim that acting upon the apparent meanings of the Book and the Sunnah is one of the roots of disbelief, is entirely false and without foundation.

The apparent meaning of the verse is far from what he supposed. Rather, the notion he imagined and the claim he asserted are not indicated by the verse at all, neither by direct implication (*mutabaqah*), nor by inclusion (*tadammun*), nor by necessary implication (*iltizam*), let alone that it should be apparent in them.

The occasion of its revelation makes this clearer, for the reason the verse was revealed is that the disbelievers asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about the Spirit, the People of the Cave and Dhu al-Qarnayn. He said to them, "I will inform you tomorrow," and he did not say, "If Allah wills." So his Lord rebuked him for not leaving the matter to Him and for not making it dependent on His will, exalted is He, and the revelation was delayed from him.

Then Allah taught him, in the verse, the etiquette to observe with Him, in His saying: ﴿And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow," unless [adding], "If Allah wills"﴾ [Al-Kahf: 23-24].

Then He said to His Prophet: ﴿And remember your Lord when you forget﴾ [Al-Kahf: 24]. This means: if you say, "I will do such-and-such tomorrow," and then forget to say, "If Allah wills," and then remember afterwards, then remember your Lord, that is, say, "If Allah wills," so that you may make up, by this, the etiquette with Allah which you missed at its proper time because of forgetfulness, and so that you may be released from the obligation of the prohibition in His saying: ﴿And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow," unless [adding], "If Allah wills."﴾

The making of the exception with this later will, for the meaning mentioned, which is the sound apparent meaning of the verse, contradicts none of the four *madhhabs* nor anyone else. It is also the verification of what is transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas concerning the permissibility of delaying the exception, as the great exegete Abu Ja'far Ibn Jarir al-Tabari, may Allah have mercy on him, explained.

We have already presented its clarification in our discussion of this verse of al-Kahf. So O followers of al-Sawi who blindly imitate him in blind ignorance: where does the apparent meaning of this verse of al-Kahf indicate an oath by Allah, or by divorce, or by manumission, or by any other kind of oath?

Did the Prophet (ﷺ) swear when he said to the disbelievers, "I will inform you tomorrow"?

Did Allah say, "And never say of anything, 'Indeed, I am swearing that I will do that tomorrow'"?

From where did you bring the oath, that you said the apparent meaning of the Qur'an is the resolution of oaths by a later exception, and on that basis you built the claim that the apparent meaning of the verse contradicts the positions of the four Imams, and that acting upon the apparent meanings of the Book and the Sunnah is one of the roots of disbelief?

What further clarifies what we have mentioned is what al-Sawi also said in Surah Al 'Imran, in his commentary on Allah's words: ﴿As for those in whose hearts is deviation, they follow that of it which is unspecific, seeking discord and seeking its interpretation, but no one knows its interpretation﴾ [Al 'Imran: 7]. He said, on the words of al-Jalal, the following text: "Zaygh means inclination away from truth toward falsehood. His words, 'by their falling into doubts and confusion,' i.e., like the Christians of Najran, and whoever follows their course among those who take the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, for the scholars have mentioned that among the roots of disbelief is taking the apparent meanings of the Book and the Sunnah." End of quotation.

So reflect, may Allah have mercy on you, on how shameful this statement is, how false it is, and how audacious its author is in violating the sanctities of Allah, His Book, His Prophet and his Sunnah (ﷺ). It also shows how clearly its author does not know what he is saying. He made what the Christians of Najran said the apparent meaning of the Book of Allah, and on that basis he made those who follow their course people who take the apparent meaning of the Qur'an.

He also mentioned that the scholars said: taking the apparent meanings of the Book and the Sunnah is among the roots of disbelief, even though he does not realise the meaning of the claim by the Christians of Najran that the apparent meaning of the Qur'an declared them disbelievers. Yet it is agreed that their claim that the apparent meaning of the Qur'an declared them, and those who follow their course, to be disbelievers is a valid claim. But the taking of the apparent meanings of the Book and the Sunnah is among the roots of disbelief?!

And he said before this: "It was said that the reason for its revelation is that a delegation from Najran said to the Prophet (ﷺ): 'Do you not say that 'Isa is the Spirit of Allah and His word?' He said: 'Yes.' They said: 'That is enough for us,' meaning that this was sufficient for them regarding his being the son of Allah." So the verse was revealed.

*(p. 263 – p. 268 of the source edition)*

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 47, verse 24 (part 3 of 6)**

It becomes clear that al-Sawi believes the claim of the Christians of Najran, that the apparent meaning of God's words ﴿And His word, which He cast to Maryam, and a spirit from Him﴾ [an-Nisa: 171] is that Isa is the son of God, is a valid claim. On this basis he holds that the scholars said: taking the apparent meanings (zawahir) of the Book and the Sunnah is one of the roots of disbelief (kufr).

All of this is among the most abominable and greatest falsehood. The verse is not understood from its apparent meaning in any way at all, nor by any indication of the indications, that Isa is the son of God. The claim of the Christians of Najran in this respect is pure lying.

So al-Sawi's statement, like that of the Christians of Najran and whoever follows their path among those who take the apparent meanings of the Qur'an, is explicit that he believes what the delegation of Najran claimed, that Isa is the son of God, is the apparent meaning of the Qur'an. This belief is utterly false, false, false. The Glorious Qur'an is too exalted for this manifest disbelief to be its apparent meaning. Rather, it does not indicate it at all, let alone being its apparent meaning.

As for His words ﴿and a spirit from Him﴾, they are like His words ﴿And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, all of it from Him﴾ [al-Jathiya: 13]. That is, all of this, from Isa and from the subjugation of the heavens and the earth, has its origin and source from Him, exalted is He.

Thus the particle "min" (from) in both verses denotes the starting point (ibtida' al-ghayah). This is the apparent meaning of the Qur'an and it is the truth, in contrast to what al-Sawi claimed and related from the Christians of Najran.

It has become clear from what we have mentioned that those who say that taking the apparent meanings of the Book and the Sunnah is one of the roots of disbelief do not know what the apparent meanings are. They believe something to be the apparent meaning of the text when the text does not indicate it in any way at all, let alone being its apparent meaning.

They built falsehood upon falsehood, and there is no doubt that falsehood is built upon only falsehood.

Had they grasped the meanings of the apparent meanings of the Book and the Sunnah as they truly are, this would have prevented them from saying what they said.

Al-Sawi's conception that the apparent meaning of the verse of al-Kahf mentioned earlier is the dissolution of oaths, by making them conditional upon the will (of God), whose time comes after the oath, and his building upon that the opposition of the apparent meaning of the verse to the positions of the Four Imams, and that taking the apparent meanings of the Book and the Sunnah is one of the roots of disbelief, [is wrong], even though the verse does not point at all to what he believed to be its apparent meaning. (p-269)

Likewise, his belief that the apparent meaning of the mentioned verse of Al 'Imran is what the Christians of Najran claimed, that Isa is the son of God, is entirely false. None of what he claimed is the apparent meaning of the Qur'an at all, as is not hidden from any intelligent person.

Al-Sawi's statement in his aforementioned remarks on Surat Al 'Imran, that the scholars said: taking the apparent meanings of the Book and the Sunnah is one of the roots of disbelief, is a false statement, and no one with even a minimal knowledge would doubt its falsehood.

Who are the scholars who said that taking the apparent meanings of the Book and the Sunnah is one of the roots of disbelief?

Name them for us, and explain to us who they are.

The truth about which there is no doubt is that this statement is not said by any scholar or any student of knowledge, because the apparent meanings of the Book and the Sunnah are the light of God which He sent down upon His Messenger, so that by it one may be guided on His earth, His limits may be upheld, His commands may be carried out, and justice may be done among His servants on His earth.

Definitive texts (nusus qat'iyyah), which admit of no possibility of another meaning, are very few; of them there are only very few examples, such as His words ﴿So a fast of three days during the Hajj and seven when you return; that is ten complete﴾ [al-Baqara: 196].

What is dominant, meaning the majority, is that the texts of the Book and the Sunnah are apparent (zawahir).

The entire Muslim community has agreed that acting upon the apparent meaning is obligatory until there comes a valid legal proof that diverts it to a less probable possibility. Every one who has spoken on the principles (usul) of jurisprudence agrees on this.

So, to repel people and keep them away from the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger, on the pretext that taking their apparent meanings is one of the roots of disbelief, is among the most abominable and greatest falsehood, as you see. (p-270)

It is obligatory upon every Muslim to beware of the roots of disbelief with utmost caution, to keep as far away from them as possible, and to avoid their causes entirely. Therefore, it follows from this hateful, abominable statement that it is obligatory to keep away from taking the apparent meanings of the Revelation.

This is as you see. And from what we have mentioned it becomes clear that among the greatest causes of misguidance is the claim that the apparent meanings of the Book and the Sunnah indicate abhorrent meanings that are not fitting.

In reality, they are far removed from and innocent of such things.

The cause of that abominable claim about the apparent meanings of the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger is that its proponents do not know.

Because of this great calamity and this supreme catastrophe, many of the theologians (nuzzar) who have understanding claimed that the apparent meanings of the verses and hadiths about the divine attributes are not fitting for God, because their apparent meanings, which come to mind first, are the likening of God's attributes to the attributes of His creation. Al-Muqri has set this out in his Idaa'ah in his statement:

"If the text gives the impression of what is unfitting for God, such as likeness to creatures, then turn it away from its apparent meaning by consensus, and cut off the hopes of what is impossible."

This false claim is among the greatest slander against the verses of God, exalted is He, and the hadiths of His Messenger ﷺ.

In reality, the apparent meanings of the verses and hadiths of the attributes, which come to the mind of every Muslim who uses his reason, contradict the attributes of God to the attributes of His creation. We must inquire here, and we say:

Does the apparent meaning that comes to mind not involve the opposition of the Creator to the created, in essence, attributes, and acts?

The answer that has no other answer is: Yes.

Is the attribute of God similar to the attributes of His creation, so that it could be said that the word indicating His attribute, exalted is He, has an apparent meaning that comes to mind as likening Him to the attribute of creation? (p-271)

The answer that has no other answer is: No.

In what way could any intelligent person imagine that a word which God sent down in His Book, for example, indicating an attribute of God by which He praised Himself, would have an apparent meaning that comes to mind as resembling the attribute of creation? ﴿Glory be to You! This is a great slander﴾ [an-Nur: 16].

So the Creator and the created are utterly different, and their attributes are utterly different.

In what way can it be conceived that the attribute of the created enters into the word indicating the attribute of the Creator? Or that the attribute of the Creator enters into the word indicating the attribute of the created, given the complete incompatibility between the Creator and the created?

Thus every word that indicates an attribute of the Creator has an apparent meaning that comes to mind which must be fitting for the Creator, free from resemblance to the attributes of the created.

Likewise, the word indicating an attribute of the created cannot be conceived to include an attribute of the Creator.

So the apparent meaning that comes to mind from the word "yad" (hand) in relation to the created is that it is a limb, consisting of bone, flesh, and blood. This is what comes to mind in such words as His saying ﴿So cut off their hands﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 38].

The apparent meaning that comes to mind from "yad" in relation to the Creator, as in His words ﴿What prevented you from prostrating to what I created with My two hands?﴾ [Sad: 75], is that it is an attribute of perfection and majesty, fitting for God, exalted is He, established for Him in the manner fitting to His perfection and majesty.

He, exalted is He, has made clear the greatness of this attribute and what it has of perfection and majesty, and He made clear that it is an attribute of influence like power. He said, exalted is He, in magnifying its rank: ﴿They did not measure God with His true measure; the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded up in His right hand. Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate﴾ [az-Zumar: 67]. (p-272)

He also made clear that it is an attribute of influence like power, in His words ﴿He said: O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to what I created with My two hands?﴾. His explicit statement that He created His prophet Adam with this great attribute, which is among the attributes of His perfection and majesty, indicates that it is among the attributes of influence, as you see.

Interpreting "yad" as "power" is not valid here at all, because the people of truth and falsehood alike agree that it is not permissible to make "power" dual.

Nor does it come to the mind of a Muslim who uses his reason that the limb, which is bone, flesh, and blood, enters into the meaning of this word, which indicates this great attribute of the Creator of the heavens and the earth.

So know, O claimant, that the apparent meaning of the word "yad" in the mentioned verse and its like is not fitting for God, because its apparent meaning is likeness to the limb of a human, and that it must be turned away from this evil apparent meaning. You did not stop at this but claimed a consensus for turning it away from its apparent meaning. Your statement is all a great slander against God, exalted is He, and against His mighty Book, and by it you became the greatest of those who liken and corporealize God. The evil of this likening has dragged you into the pit of negation (ta'til). So you denied the attribute which God affirmed for Himself in His Book, on the claim that it is not fitting for Him, and you interpreted it with another meaning from your own accord, without any basis from the Book, the Sunnah, consensus, or the words of any of the early predecessors (salaf).

What harm would come to you if you were truthful to God and believed in what He praised Himself with, in the manner fitting to His perfection and majesty, without asking how, without likening, and without negation?

And by what justification did you allow your mind to let the attribute of the created come to it when the attribute of the Creator is mentioned?

Does the attribute of the Creator become confused with the attribute of the created for anyone, so that he understands the attribute of the created from the word indicating the attribute of the Creator?

So fear God, O human, and beware of speaking about God without knowledge, and believe in what came in the Book of God while declaring God free from resemblance to His creation.

Know that God, whose knowledge encompasses everything, is not hidden from Him is the difference between the attribute fitting to Him and the attribute not fitting to Him, so that a person would come and arbitrarily decide about it, saying: "This which you described yourself with is not fitting for you, and I negate it from you without any basis from you or from your Messenger, and I will bring you in its place an attribute fitting for you." (p-273)

So "yad," for example, with which you described yourself, is not fitting for you because it indicates likeness to a limb. I negate it from you definitively, and I substitute for it for you an attribute fitting for you, which is blessing, or power, for example, or generosity.

﴿Glory be to You! This is a great slander.﴾

﴿So fear God, O people of understanding, who believe. God has sent down to you a reminder, a Messenger who recites to you the signs of God made clear, to bring out those who believe and do righteous deeds from the darknesses into the light﴾ [at-Talaq: 10–11].

Strangely, some of those who deny God's attributes and interpret them with meanings that did not come from God or from His Messenger believe in some of the Book and not in others.

They acknowledge that the seven attributes from which derivatives are formed are established for God with transcendence (tanzih). We mean by them power, will, knowledge, life, hearing, sight, and speech, because from them are derived "Capable," "Living," "Knowing," and so on. Likewise, with some comprehensive attributes such as greatness, pride, sovereignty, and majesty, for example, because from them are derived "the Great," "the Proud," "the Majestic," and "the King." And so they deny every attribute that is established in the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ from which no other derivative is formed, such as the attributes of hand, face, and the like. There is no doubt that this distinction between the attributes of God, which He affirmed for Himself or which His Messenger ﷺ affirmed for Him, has no basis whatsoever in any way.

Nor did any permission come from God or from His Messenger ﷺ to believe in some of His attributes while denying and interpreting others, on the grounds that they do not produce derivatives.

Can any intelligent person imagine that the absence of derivation is a justification for denying what God described Himself with?

There is no doubt for any Muslim who uses his reason that the absence of derivation does not render invalid the words of God about what He praised Himself with, nor the words of His Messenger about what he described his Lord with.

The reason that obliges belief absolutely and universally is that it comes from God. This is the reason that those firmly rooted in knowledge know to be the cause obliging belief in everything that comes from God, whether God has kept its knowledge to Himself, as with the ambiguous (mutashabih), or it is among what those firmly rooted in knowledge know, as God said about them: ﴿And those firmly rooted in knowledge say: We believe in it; all of it is from our Lord﴾ [Al 'Imran: 7]. (p-274)

There is no doubt that His saying, ﴿with what I created with My two hands﴾, is from our Lord, and His saying, ﴿And Allah is over all things competent﴾ [al-Baqarah: 284], is also from our Lord. Therefore it is obligatory for us to believe in all of it, because all of it is from our Lord.

As for the one who distinguishes between them, while knowing that all of it is from his Lord, by claiming that this part is subject to interpretation (*ishtiqaq*) and that part is not, he has believed in some of the Book and rejected some of it.

What is intended is that everything that has come from Allah must be believed in, whether it is among the *mutashabih* (ambiguous verses) or not among the *mutashabih*, and whether or not it is subject to *ishtiqaq*.

It is well known that Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, was asked, "How did He establish Himself (*istawa*)?" He said: "The *istiwa'* is not unknown, the *kayf* (modality) is not conceivable, belief in it is obligatory, and asking about it is an innovation."

As for the claim of some people that power, will and similar attributes are not like the hand and the face, on the pretext that the effects of power and will appear in the higher and lower worlds, unlike other attributes such as the attribute of the hand and the like, this is among the greatest falsehoods.

Among what clarifies this is that what he and his father and his grandfather say is itself one of the effects of the attribute of the hand, with which Allah created His prophet Adam.

We hope that Allah, exalted is He, will forgive those who died holding this belief, because they do not intend to liken Allah to His creation; rather, they try to declare Him free from resemblance to His creation.

Their intention is good, but their path to that intention is evil.

That evil arose for them only because they thought that the wording of the attribute by which Allah praised Himself, in its apparent meaning, indicates resemblance to the attributes of creation. So they negated the attribute, which they thought was unfitting, intending thereby to declare Allah free from it, and they interpreted it with another meaning which, in their opinion, required transcendence. They are, as al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

*He sought a benefit but caused harm unintentionally,*
*and from righteousness there is that which becomes disobedience.*

We hope that Allah will forgive their error and that they are among those referred to in His saying: (p-275) ﴿And there is no blame upon you for what you have done in error, but what your hearts intended. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Ahzab: 5].

Their aforementioned error is beyond doubt. Had Allah guided them to purify their hearts from *tashbih* (likening Allah to creation) first, and had they been certain that the apparent meaning of the attribute of the Creator is that He is declared free from resemblance to the attributes of the created, they would have been safe from what they fell into.

There is no doubt that the Prophet ﷺ knew fully that the apparent and immediately understood meaning of what Allah praised Himself with in the verses of the attributes is the complete declaration of His freedom from the attributes of creation.
