Had it occurred to his mind that the apparent meaning was unfitting, because it would be likening Him to the attributes of creation, he would have hastened fully to explain that, because it is not permissible for him to delay clarification beyond the time of need, especially in matters of belief, and especially concerning what apparently implies disbelief and likening.

Therefore the silence of the Prophet ﷺ about explaining this indicates that what the interpreters claimed has no basis, as you see.

If it is said: This great Qur'an was revealed in a clear Arabic tongue, and the Arabs do not know in their language a *kayfiyyah* (modality) for the hand, for example, except the modalities of meanings known to them, such as the limb and other known meanings of "hand" in the language. So explain to us a modality for the hand that suits what you have mentioned.

The answer has two aspects.

The first aspect: The Arabs do not grasp the modalities of Allah's attributes through their language, because of the strong incompatibility of Allah's attributes with the attributes of creation.

The Arabs' minds only recognize modalities for the attributes of creation. So the Arabs do not know a modality for hearing and sight except the observed form in the organs of the ear and the eye. As for a hearing that does not subsist in an ear, or a sight that does not subsist in a pupil, they do not know any modality for it at all.

So there is no difference between hearing and sight on the one hand, and the hand and the *istiwa'* on the other. What the Arabs know, from their language, of all of that is what is observed in created things.

(p-276) As for what Allah has attributed to Himself of these, the Arabs know no modality for it, nor any limit to the difference between His attributes and the attributes of creation. However, they know from their language the basic meaning, as the Imam Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "The *istiwa'* is not unknown, the *kayf* is not conceivable, belief in it is obligatory, and asking about it is an innovation."

They also know from their language that between the Creator and the created, the provider and the provided, the giver of life and the one who receives life, and the giver of death and the one who dies, there are enormous differences without limit, which necessitate complete dissimilarity between the attributes of the Creator and the created.

The second aspect: We say to the one who says, "Explain to us a modality for the hand that suits what you have mentioned, namely that it is an attribute of perfection and majesty, declared free from resemblance to the limb of the created":

Have you come to know the modality of the sacred Essence that is described as having a hand? He must say, "No." If he says that,

we say: Knowing the modality of the attributes depends on knowing the modality of the Essence.

The Essence and the attributes are of one category.

Just as His Essence, majestic and exalted is He, is unlike all essences, so His attributes are unlike all attributes.

It is well known that attributes differ and vary according to the things they are attributed to.

Do you not see, for example, that the word *ra's* (head) is a single word?

If you attach it to a human, you say *ra's al-insan* (the head of the human); if to a valley, *ra's al-wadi* (the head of the valley); if to money, *ra's al-mal* (the capital); and if to a mountain, *ra's al-jabal* (the peak of the mountain).

The meanings of the word *ra's* differ and vary greatly according to the difference in what it is attached to, even though these are all lowly created things.

(p-277) So what of the attributes attributed to Allah, and what is attributed to His creation? They differ just as the Creator differs from the created, as is clear.

It has become evident from what has been mentioned that the condition in the saying of al-Muqri in his *Idā'ah* (Exposition):

*And the text, if it gives the impression of what is unfitting,*

is definitely a condition that does not exist, because the texts of revelation that come concerning the attributes of Allah do not, in their apparent meanings, indicate anything at all except the declaration of Allah's freedom from resemblance to His creation, and His difference from His creation in His Essence, attributes and actions.

Therefore, every Muslim who examines his intellect will not doubt that the apparent and immediately understood meaning that comes to the mind of a Muslim is the difference of Allah from His creation, as He affirmed in His saying: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [al-Shura: 11], and His saying: ﴿And there is none comparable to Him﴾ [al-Ikhlas: 4], and similar verses.

From this you know that the consensus which he built on that in his saying:

*So turn it away from its apparent meaning by consensus,*

is a consensus that is absolutely non-existent and has no existence at all, because it is based on a condition that does not exist at all.

So the non-existent consensus that is claimed did not come in the Book of Allah, nor in the Sunnah of His Messenger, nor did any of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah say it, nor any of their Successors, nor any of the four Imams, nor any of the well-known jurists of the regions.

They did not say it only because they know that the apparent meanings of the texts of revelation indicate nothing except the declaration of Allah's freedom from resemblance to His creation, and this apparent meaning, which is the declaration of Allah's transcendence, has no reason to turn it away from that, as you see.

For all of this we have said in the introduction to this blessed book: Indeed Allah, blessed and exalted is He, is described (p-278) with those attributes in reality, not metaphorically, because we firmly believe, without any doubt entering it, that the apparent meanings of the verses and hadiths of the attributes do not indicate at all anything except the declaration of freedom from resemblance to the created, and His being described, exalted is He, with perfection and majesty.

Affirming transcendence, perfection and majesty for Allah in reality and not metaphorically is not denied by any Muslim.

What calls for explicitly using the term *haqiqah* (literal reality) and negating *majaz* (figurative usage) is the great number of ignorant people who claim that those attributes have no realities, and that they are all figurative usages.

They made this a way to negate them, because a figurative usage may be negated, but a literal reality may not be negated.

So they said, for example: The hand is a figurative usage, meaning by it power, favour or generosity; so they negated the attribute of the hand, because it is figurative.

And they said: "*ʿAla al-ʿarshi istawa*" (He established Himself upon the Throne) is figurative, so they negated the *istiwa'*, because it is figurative.

And they said: The meaning of "*istawa*" is "*istawla*" (took control), and they likened His control to the control of Bishr ibn Marwan over Iraq.

Had they contemplated the Book of Allah, it would have prevented them from replacing *istiwa'* with *istila'* and replacing the hand with power or favour. For Allah, exalted is He, says in His decisive Book in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿But those who did wrong changed the word to other than that which had been said to them. So We sent upon the wrongdoers a plague from the sky because they were defiantly disobedient﴾ [al-Baqarah: 59], and He says in al-A'raf: ﴿But those who did wrong among them changed the word to other than that which had been said to them. So We sent upon them a plague from the sky because they had been wronging﴾ [al-A'raf: 162]. The word that Allah had said to them was *ḥiṭṭah* (remission), which is a noun from *ḥaṭṭ* meaning "putting down," predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: our supplication and our request to You is *ḥiṭṭah* for our sins, i.e., a removal and putting down of them from us. So it means seeking forgiveness. In some narrations of the hadith about them it is stated that they changed this word by adding a *nūn*, saying *ḥinṭah*, which is wheat.

As for the people of ta'wil (figurative interpretation), it was said to them: *ʿAla al-ʿarshi istawa*, but they added a *lām*, saying *istawla*.

(p-279) This *lām* that they added is most like the *nūn* that the Jews added in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And say, "ḥiṭṭah"﴾. And Allah, exalted is He, says in forbidding the replacement of the Qur'an with other than it: ﴿Say, "It is not for me to change it on my own accord. I only follow what is revealed to me. Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a great Day."﴾

There is no doubt that whoever changes *istawa* to *istawla*, for example, has not followed what was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ.

So he must avoid changing and fear the great punishment, which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ feared if he disobeyed Allah by replacing the Qur'an with something other than it, as mentioned in His saying: ﴿Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a great Day.﴾

The Jews did not deny that the word Allah said to them was the word *ḥiṭṭah*, but they distorted it by the aforementioned addition.

And the people of this view did not deny that the word of the Qur'an is *istawa*, but they distorted it and said about its meaning: *istawla*. They replaced it with that because, in their opinion, it is more appropriate than the word of the Qur'an, since the word of the Qur'an gives the impression of what is unfitting, whereas the word *istawla*, in their opinion, is the one that declares Allah free and is fitting for Allah. Yet no likening is more abominable than likening the control of Allah over His supposed Throne to the control of a man over Iraq.

Was there anyone who contested Allah over His Throne, so that He overcame him and took control of the Throne?

Is there anything over which Allah does not have control? Allah has control over everything.

Is it permissible to say that He established Himself over everything other than the Throne?

Understand this.

(p-280) In any case, the interpreter claimed that *istiwa'* gives the impression of what is unfitting for Allah, because it implies resembling the *istiwa'* of creation, and he brought *istila'* instead of it, because in his claim it is the fitting one for Him. But he did not notice that

likening Allah's control over His Throne to the control of Bishr ibn Marwan over Iraq is the most monstrous kind of likening, and certainly not fitting. Yet he says that the supposed control is free from resemblance to the control of creatures, although he gave the example of it as the control of Bishr over Iraq. And Allah says: ﴿So do not strike examples for Allah. Indeed, Allah knows, and you do not know﴾ [al-Nahl: 74].

We say: O interpreter, with this interpretation of yours, we ask you: if you know that one of the two wordings must be declared free from likeness, namely the word *istawa*, which Allah sent down with the angel upon the Prophet ﷺ as a Qur'an that is recited, each letter of which carries ten good deeds, and whoever denies that it is from the Book of Allah has disbelieved,

and the word *istawla*, which people brought from their own accord without relying on any text from the Book of Allah, nor the Sunnah of His Messenger, nor the saying of any of the early generations, then which of the two should be declared free from likeness?

Which of the two words, in your opinion, is more deserving of being declared free from defect? Is it the word of the Qur'an, sent down by Allah upon His Messenger, or your word which you have brought forth from your own selves, without any basis whatsoever?

The correct answer to this question is not hidden from us, if you do not know it.

Know that what we have mentioned, namely that whatever attributes Allah has described Himself with, He is described with them in their literal sense, not figuratively, in the manner befitting His perfection and majesty,

and that there is absolutely no difference between an attribute from which a derived description is formed, such as hearing, sight and life,

and an attribute from which no such derivation is formed, such as face and hand,

and that interpreting the attributes, like interpreting "istiwa'" as "istila'" (taking control), is neither permissible nor valid.

This is the creed of Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, may Allah have mercy on him.

It is also the creed of the majority of the Salaf, and what the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions followed.

Whoever claims against Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari that he interprets any of the attributes, such as the face, the hand, istiwa' and the like, has spoken a tremendous falsehood against him.

(p-281) Rather, al-Ash'ari, may Allah have mercy on him, explicitly states in his great books that he composed after returning from Mu'tazilism (such as al-Mujaz, Maqalat al-Islamiyyin wa Ikhtilaf al-Musallin, and al-Ibana 'an Usul al-Diyana) that his creed by which he worships Allah is what the righteous Salaf held: belief in everything Allah described Himself with, or His Messenger ﷺ described Him with, and affirming all of it without modality (kayf), without likening (tashbih), and without negation (ta'til).

And that such attributes may not be interpreted, nor is figurative meaning (majaz) to be asserted regarding them.

And that interpreting istiwa' as istila' is the doctrine of the Mu'tazilah and those who resemble them.

He was the most knowledgeable of people regarding the sayings of the Mu'tazilah, because he had been the greatest imam in their school before Allah guided him to the truth. We shall mention here some of the texts of Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, may Allah have mercy on him, so that you may know the soundness of what we have mentioned about him.

He, may Allah have mercy on him, said in the Kitab al-Ibana 'an Usul al-Diyana, which many have said was the last book he wrote, the following text:

"If someone says to us: You have denied the saying of the Mu'tazilah, the Qadariyyah, the Jahmiyyah, the Harouriyyah, the Rafidah and the Murji'ah, so define for us your saying by which you speak and your religion by which you follow, it is said to him:

Our saying which we speak and our religion which we follow is adherence to the Book of our Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, and the Sunnah of our Prophet ﷺ, and what has been narrated from the Companions, the Followers, and the imams of hadith.

We hold fast to that, and we speak in accordance with what Abu 'Abd Allah Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Hanbal used to say, may Allah make his face radiant, raise his rank and magnify his reward, and we keep away from whoever opposes his saying.

For he was the excellent imam and the complete leader, through whom Allah made the truth clear, lifted misguidance, clarified the path, suppressed the innovations of the innovators, the deviation of the deviant and the doubt of the doubters. So may the mercy of Allah be upon him, from an imam who is honored and a friend who is esteemed and exalted, and upon all the imams of the Muslims.

The summary of our saying is: we affirm Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and what has come from Allah, and what the trustworthy narrators have related from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; we reject none of that.

That Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is one God, there is no god but Him, the One, the Eternal Refuge, who has not taken a consort nor a son; and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, whom He sent with guidance and the religion of truth; that Paradise is true, that Hellfire is true, that the Hour is coming with no doubt about it, and that Allah will resurrect those in the graves.

(p-282) That Allah istawa over His Throne as He said: "The Most Merciful istawa over the Throne" [Ta-Ha: 5]; that He has a face as He said: "And there remains the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor" [Ar-Rahman: 27]; that He has two hands without modality as He said: "I created with My Two Hands" [Sad: 75], and as He said: "Rather, both His Hands are outstretched" [Al-Ma'idah: 64]; and that He has two eyes without modality as He said: "Sailing under Our eyes" [Al-Qamar: 14]." End of the relevant portion of his words.

By this you know that whoever slanders al-Ash'ari, claiming that he is among the interpreters who assert that the apparent meaning of the verses and hadiths about the attributes is unfitting for Allah, is lying against him with a grievous lie.

Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari also said in the Kitab al-Ibana, in affirming istiwa' for Allah, the Exalted, the following text:

"If someone says: What do you say about istiwa'? It is said to him: We say that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is istawa over His Throne as He said: 'The Most Merciful istawa over the Throne.' Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has said: 'To Him ascends the good word' [Fatir: 10], and He has said: 'Rather, Allah raised him to Himself' [An-Nisa': 158], and He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'He arranges the affair from the heaven to the earth; then it ascends to Him' [As-Sajdah: 5], and He related about Pharaoh: 'O Haman, build for me a tower that I may reach the means, the means to the heavens, and look at the God of Moses; and indeed, I think he is a liar' [Ghafir: 36].

So Pharaoh denied the Prophet of Allah Moses, peace be upon him, in his saying that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is above the heavens. And He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Are you secure that He who is in the heaven will not cause the earth to swallow you?'

Above the heavens is the Throne; and since the Throne is above the heavens, He said: 'He who is in the heaven,' because He is istawa over the Throne which is above the heavens, and everything that is elevated is called a heaven, so the Throne is the highest of the heavens." This is the wording of Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, may Allah have mercy on him, in the aforementioned Kitab al-Ibana.

He, may Allah have mercy on him, extended his discussion by citing Qur'anic evidences for affirming the attribute of istiwa' and the attribute of highness (uluww) for Allah, Exalted is He.

From the body of his aforementioned speech is the following text:

(p-283) "Some of the Mu'tazilah, the Jahmiyyah and the Harouriyyah have said: The saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, 'The Most Merciful istawa over the Throne' means that He took control, reigned and subdued. They claim that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is in every place. They denied that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is over His Throne as the people of truth say, and they took istiwa' to mean power (qudrah).

If this were as they claimed, there would be no difference between the Throne and the earth, for Allah, Glorified is He, has power over them and over the latrines, and over everything in the world.

So if Allah were istawa over the Throne in the sense of istila', while He, the Mighty and Majestic, has control over all things, He would then be istawa over the Throne, over the earth, over the heaven, over the latrines and over the privies, because He has power over things and has control over them.

And since He has power over all things, and no Muslim has permitted saying that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is istawa over latrines and privies, it is not permissible that istiwa' over the Throne be the sense of istila' which is general over all things.

It is necessary that its meaning be an istiwa' specific to the Throne, not to all things.

The Mu'tazilah, the Harouriyyah and the Jahmiyyah claimed that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is in every place, so it necessarily follows that He is in the belly of Mary and in the latrines and privies.

This is contrary to religion; Exalted is Allah above their saying." End of quotation.

This is the wording of Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, may Allah have mercy on him, in the last of his works, the Kitab al-Ibana 'an Usul al-Diyana.

And you see that he explicitly stated that interpreting istiwa' as istila' is the saying of the Mu'tazilah, the Jahmiyyah and the Harouriyyah, and not the saying of anyone from the People of the Sunnah; and he established clear proofs for the falsity of that.

So let those who interpret istiwa' as istila' know that their predecessors in this are the Mu'tazilah, the Jahmiyyah and the Harouriyyah, not Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, may Allah have mercy on him, nor any of the Salaf.

We have already explained in Surah al-An'am, in discussing His saying, "And He is Allah in the heavens and in the earth; He knows your secret and your open" [Al-An'am: 3], that the saying of the Jahmiyyah and those who follow them, "Allah is in every place," is a false saying.

(p-284) Because all existing places are too lowly, too small and too insignificant for anything of them to contain the Creator of the heavens and the earth, who is greater and larger than everything, who encompasses everything, and whom nothing encompasses.

Look at the clarification of that in al-An'am.

Know that what many of the ignorant claim, that what is in the Great Qur'an of the attribute of istiwa', highness and aboveness necessitates a direction (jihah), and that this is impossible for Allah, and that it is obligatory to negate istiwa', highness and aboveness and interpret them by meanings for which there is no evidence, is entirely false.

Its cause is bad opinion of Allah and His Book. In any case, whoever claims that the apparent texts of the Great Qur'an necessitate direction, and that this implication entails a deficiency requiring interpretation, is asked:

What do you mean by direction?

If you mean by direction an existing place in which Allah is confined, this is not the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, and no Muslim has said it.

And if you mean by direction pure non-existence,

then non-existence is an expression for nothing.

So first distinguish between an existing thing and nothing.

Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, may Allah have mercy on him, also said in the Kitab al-Ibana, also, the following text:

"If we are asked: Do you say that Allah has two hands? It is said: We say that, and His saying, the Mighty and Majestic, 'The hand of Allah is above their hands' [Al-Fath: 10] indicates it, and His saying, the Mighty and Majestic, 'For what I created with My two hands' [Sad: 75]."

He, may Allah have mercy on him, extended the discussion in citing the evidences from the Book and the Sunnah for establishing the attribute of two hands for Allah.

From the body of what he said is the following text:

"It is said to them: Why do you deny that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, meant by His saying 'My two hands' two hands that are not blessings?

If they say: Because a hand, if it is not a blessing, is nothing but a limb.

(p-285) It is said to them: And why have you decided that a hand, if it is not a blessing, is nothing but a limb?

Is it not that our return is to what we witness and what we find among creatures?

They say: A hand, if it is not a blessing in what is witnessed, is nothing but a limb.

It is said to them: If you act upon what is witnessed and judge Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, by it, then likewise we have not found any living creature except a body of flesh and blood, so judge Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, by that.

Otherwise, you are interpreters of your own saying and contradictors of your own reasoning.

And if you affirm a living being unlike the living beings among us,

why do you deny that the two hands about which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, informed us are two hands that are not blessings, nor limbs, nor like hands?

Likewise it is said to them:

You did not find a wise governor except a human; then you affirmed that the world has a wise governor, unlike a human, and you opposed what is witnessed and broke your own reasoning.

So do not prevent the affirmation of two hands that are not blessings nor limbs, on the ground that this contradicts what is witnessed." End of the relevant portion of his words.

By this you know that al-Ash'ari, may Allah have mercy on him, believes that the attributes which the interpreters have denied, such as the attribute of the hand, are among the attributes of meaning like life and the like, and that there is absolutely no difference between the attribute of the hand and the attribute of life. So whatever Allah is described with of all that is free from resemblance to what creatures are described with of it.

What is necessary for whoever likens in some attributes and negates in others is that he must liken in all of them or negate in all of them, as al-Ash'ari said.

As for the claim that likeness appears in some of them but not others, there is no basis for it in any way whatsoever, because the One described by them is one, and He is free from resembling the attributes of His creatures.

And from the body of the words of Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned just above, in establishing the attributes, is the following text:

(p-286) "If someone says: Why do you deny that His saying, 'What our hands have done' [Ya-Sin: 71], and His saying, 'For what I created with My two hands' [Sad: 75], be figurative?

It is said to him: The ruling of the speech of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is that it be on its apparent and literal meaning, and nothing departs from its apparent meaning to figurative meaning except by a proof.

Do you not see that if the apparent meaning of speech is generality, and it comes in a general expression while the intended meaning is specificity, then it is not in the literal sense of the apparent meaning?"

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 47, verse 24 (part 6 of 6):

It is not permissible to depart from what is apparently general to something other than the general sense without evidence?
Likewise the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿That which I created with My two hands﴾ is to be taken in its apparent and literal sense, affirming two hands. It is not permissible to depart from the apparent meaning of "two hands" to what our opponents claim, except with evidence.
If that were permitted to any claimant, so that he could say that what is apparently general is particular, and what is apparently particular is general, without evidence,
then, since this is not permitted to the one who claims it without proof, it is not permitted to you to claim that it is figurative (majāz, non-literal usage) without evidence.
Rather, it is obligatory that His saying ﴿That which I created with My two hands﴾ affirms two hands for Allah, Exalted, in the literal sense (ḥaqīqah), not two blessings, since, according to the people of the language, it is not permitted for a speaker to say "I did it with my two hands" while meaning two blessings. The purpose of the quotation ends here, in his words.
In this there is an explicit statement of Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, may Allah have mercy on him, that the attributes of Allah, like the attribute of the hand, are established for Him in the literal sense and not figuratively, and that those who claim they are figurative are his opponents, and he is their opponent, as you see.
He, may Allah have mercy on him, only said that He, Exalted, is characterized by them in the literal sense and not figuratively, because there is no doubt that the apparent meaning of an attribute of Allah is its difference from the attributes of creation, and its transcendence above resembling them, as is the practice of all the pious predecessors (al-salaf al-ṣāliḥ).
Thus, affirming the literal sense and negating the figurative in the attributes of Allah is the belief of every Muslim whose heart is pure of the filth of anthropomorphism (tashbīh, likening Allah to creation). For what comes to his mind from the word that signifies an attribute, such as the attribute of the hand or the face, is only that it is an attribute of perfection, transcendent above resembling the attributes of creation.
(p-287) So the likening that is the cause of denying the attribute and interpreting it with a meaning that has no basis does not occur to his mind.
[[The author's words have been abridged because of their great length]]

(p-379) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who turned back on their heels after guidance had become clear to them, Satan has enticed them and given them false hope.﴾ ﴿That is because they said to those who hated what Allah had sent down, "We will obey you in some matters," but Allah knows their secrets.﴾ ﴿So how will it be when the angels take them in death, striking their faces and their backs?﴾ ﴿That is because they followed what angered Allah and disliked His pleasure, so He nullified their deeds.﴾

The apparent meaning of "those who turned back on their heels after guidance had become clear to them" is a people who disbelieved after their faith.

Some scholars said: they are the Jews who used to believe in our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), but when he was sent and they confirmed that he is the Prophet described in their books, they disbelieved in him.

According to this view, their "turning back on their heels" is their disbelief in him after they had recognized and become certain of him, and on this view the guidance that became clear to them is the validity of his prophethood (ﷺ) and their knowledge of him through the signs present in their books.

On this view, this verse is clarified by His saying in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿And when there came to them a Book from Allah confirming what was with them, although previously they had been seeking victory over those who disbelieved, yet when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 89]; because His saying "when there came to them that which they recognized" explains the meaning of His saying "after guidance had become clear to them," and His saying "they disbelieved and barred you" explains the meaning of His saying "turned back on their heels."

Some scholars said: the aforementioned verse was revealed concerning the hypocrites.

In this noble verse, He, exalted and majestic, has made clear that the cause of the turning back of these people after guidance had become clear to them is the seduction of Satan, as He, exalted, said, pointing to the reason for that: ﴿Satan has enticed them,﴾ meaning he made disbelief and apostasy from the religion appealing to them; ﴿and given them false hope,﴾ meaning he extended hope to them and promised them long life.

Al-Zamakhshari said: "sawwala" means he made it easy for them to undertake great matters, from "sawl," which is relaxation; and whoever derived it from "su'l" (request) has no knowledge of morphology and derivation at all; "and given them false hope" means he extended to them hopes and wishes. End of quote.

(p-380) The explanation of this is that these apostates after guidance had become clear to them, this happened to them because Satan enticed them to it, that is, he made it easy for them, adorned it for them, made it seem good to them, and promised them long lives; because the extension of hope is among the greatest causes of committing disbelief and sins.

In this word there are two canonical readings. The majority of the Seven read ﴿wa-amlā lahum﴾ with a fatḥah on the hamzah and on the lām followed by an alif; it is a past-tense verb in the active voice, and its subject is a pronoun referring to Satan.

The root meaning of imlā' is granting respite and extending the term, and from it is His saying: ﴿And I will give them respite; indeed, My plan is firm.﴾ [al-A'raf: 183], and His saying: ﴿And let not those who disbelieve think that Our giving them respite is good for them. We only give them respite so that they increase in sin.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 178].

The meaning of Satan's giving them respite is his promising them long lives, as He said: ﴿He promises them and gives them desires, but Satan promises them nothing except delusion.﴾ [al-Nisa': 120].

And He said: ﴿And incite whom you can among them with your voice... and promise them; but Satan promises them nothing except delusion.﴾ [al-Isra': 64].

Some scholars said: the subject pronoun in His saying ﴿wa-amlā lahum﴾ according to the reading of the majority refers to Allah, exalted is He.

The meaning then is: ﴿Satan has enticed them,﴾ that is, he made disbelief and sins easy for them and adorned and beautified them; and Allah, exalted and majestic, granted them respite, that is, gave them a respite of gradual seizure (istidraj).

That the enticement is from Satan and the respite is from Allah is attested by verses of the Book of Allah:

• such as His saying concerning Satan's adornment for them: ﴿And when Satan made their deeds appealing to them﴾ [al-Anfal: 48],

• and His saying: ﴿By Allah, We certainly sent to nations before you, but Satan made their deeds appealing to them; so he is their guardian today, and theirs is a painful punishment.﴾ [al-Nahl: 63],

• and His saying: ﴿And Satan will say when the matter is decided, "Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I broke it for you."﴾ [Ibrahim: 22],

and other verses.

And:

• such as His saying concerning Allah's granting them respite as gradual seizure: ﴿We will draw them gradually from where they do not know. And I will give them respite; indeed, My plan is firm.﴾ [al-Qalam: 44],

• and His saying: (p-381) ﴿And let not those who disbelieve think that Our giving them respite is good for them. We only give them respite so that they increase in sin, and for them is a humiliating punishment.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 178],

• and His saying: ﴿Say: whoever is in error, the Most Merciful will extend for him an extension﴾ [Maryam: 75],

• and His saying: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened to them the gates of everything until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and they were then in despair.﴾ [al-An'am: 44],

• and His saying: ﴿Then We replaced the bad with good until they multiplied, and said, "Indeed, hardship and ease touched our fathers," so We seized them suddenly while they did not perceive.﴾ [al-A'raf: 95],

• and His saying: ﴿Do they think that what We provide them with of wealth and children is us hastening to them with good? Rather they do not perceive.﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 55–56],

and verses of this kind are many and well known.

Abu 'Amr alone among the Seven read ﴿wa-umliya lahum﴾ with a ḍammah on the hamzah and a kasrah on the lām, followed by a fatḥah on the yā', in the past passive form with an omitted agent; the two possibilities mentioned just above regarding the subject of the majority reading apply here too.

We have already mentioned what supports each of them from the Qur'an, such as His saying concerning Satan's giving them respite: ﴿He promises them and gives them desires, but Satan promises them nothing except delusion,﴾ [al-Nisa': 120], and His saying concerning Allah's giving them respite: ﴿And I will give them respite; indeed, My plan is firm,﴾ [al-Qalam: 45], as has been mentioned shortly before.

The reference in His saying in this noble verse: ﴿That is because they said to those who hated what Allah had sent down, "We will obey you in some matters,"﴾ goes back to His saying: ﴿Satan has enticed them and given them false hope.﴾

That is, that enticement and respite, which lead to disbelief, occurred because they said to those who hated what Allah had sent down, "We will obey you in some matters."

The apparent meaning of the verse indicates that some of the matters in which they promised to obey them were from what Allah had sent down and which those obeyed ones hated.

The noble verse indicates that everyone who obeys someone who hates what Allah has sent down, by helping him in his aversion and supporting him in that falsehood, is a disbeliever in Allah, by the evidence of His saying concerning such people: ﴿So how will it be when the angels take them in death, striking their faces and their backs? That is because they followed what angered Allah and disliked His pleasure, so He nullified their deeds.﴾ [Muhammad: 27–28].

We have already set forth what clarifies this from the Qur'an in Surat al-Shura in discussing His saying (p-382) ﴿And whatever you differ about, its ruling is with Allah﴾ [al-Shura: 10], and in many other places in this blessed book.

We also explained in Surat al-Shura the intensity of the disbelievers' aversion to what Allah has sent down, and we demonstrated that with Qur'anic verses in discussing His saying: ﴿Hard for the polytheists is that to which you invite them﴾ [al-Shura: 13], and we have repeatedly stated that the lesson is in the generality of wording, not the specificity of causes.

As for His saying in this noble verse: ﴿But Allah knows their secrets,﴾ Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, Ibn 'Amir, and Shu'bah from 'Asim read ﴿asrārahum﴾ with a fatḥah on the hamzah, the plural of sirr (secret).

Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Hafs from 'Asim read ﴿isrārahum﴾ with a kasrah on the hamzah, the verbal noun of asarra, as in His saying: ﴿And I have spoken to them secretly in private﴾ [Nuh: 9]. They said this to them in secret, but Allah, who knows everything they conceal and everything they declare, made it known.

As for His saying in this noble verse: ﴿So how will it be when the angels take them in death, striking their faces and their backs?﴾ that is: how will the condition of these be when the angels take them? That is, the Angel of Death and his helpers seize their souls while they are striking their faces and their backs.

What this noble verse includes of the angels taking the disbelievers in death while striking their faces and backs has been clarified in other places in the Book of Allah, such as His saying in al-Anfal: ﴿If you could see when the angels take those who disbelieve, striking their faces and their backs﴾ [al-Anfal: 50], and His saying in al-An'am: ﴿If you could see when the wrongdoers are in the agonies of death and the angels are extending their hands, "Bring out your souls; today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation"﴾ [al-An'am: 93].

So His saying: "extending their hands" means with the striking mentioned.

The reference in His saying: ﴿That is because they followed what angered Allah﴾ goes back to the verbal noun implicit in the verb "they strike" (yadribūna), namely His saying: ﴿striking their faces and their backs.﴾ That is, that striking at the time of death occurs because of ﴿their following what angered Allah,﴾ meaning what provoked His anger, namely disbelief in Him and obedience to the disbelievers who hate what He sent down.

Al-Iskhat means seeking to bring about wrath, which here is anger.

(p-383) His saying: ﴿and disliked His pleasure﴾ — because whoever obeys someone who hates what Allah has sent down has disliked the pleasure of Allah, since His pleasure lies only in acting upon what He has sent down. So hating what He sent down entails hating His pleasure, because His pleasure is in what He sent down; and whoever obeys its hater is like its hater.

His saying: ﴿so He nullified their deeds﴾ means He made them void, because disbelief is an evil with which no good deed benefits. We have fully explained this in Surat al-Isra' in discussing His saying: ﴿And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it as due, while he is a believer — those are the ones whose striving is appreciated﴾ [al-Isra': 19], and in Surat al-Nahl in discussing His saying: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, male or female, while he is a believer — We will surely give him a good life﴾ [al-Nahl: 97].

Know that some scholars have said that this noble verse was revealed concerning the hypocrites.

Others said it was revealed concerning the Jews, and that the hypocrites or the Jews said to the disbelievers who hated what Allah had sent down, "We will obey you in some matters," namely hostility to the Prophet (ﷺ), hindering from jihad, and the like.

Some of them say that those who followed what angered Allah are the Jews when they disbelieved in the Prophet (ﷺ) after recognizing him, and disliked His pleasure, which is belief in him (ﷺ).

The indisputable verification is that these verses are general in everything their wording encompasses, and that all the threat they contain applies to whoever obeys someone who hates what Allah has sent down.

**Issue**

Know that every Muslim, in this era, must reflect on these verses of Surat Muhammad and ponder them, and must be completely cautious of the severe threat they contain, because many who ascribe themselves to the Muslims undoubtedly fall under the severe threat they contain.

This is because most disbelievers, from east and west, hate what Allah has sent down to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), which is this Qur'an and what the Prophet (ﷺ) explains of it through the Sunnah.

So whoever says to these disbelievers who hate what Allah has sent down, "We will obey you in some matters," is included in the threat of the verse.

Even more so is one who says to them, "We will obey you in the matter," like those who follow man-made laws, obeying by that those who hate what Allah has sent down; for these, without doubt, are among those whom the angels take in death, striking their faces and their backs,

and that they followed what angered Allah and disliked His pleasure, and that He will nullify their deeds.

So beware with utmost caution of entering among those who said: "We will obey you in some matters."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 47, verse 31:

The utterance of His, the Exalted: ﴿And We will surely test you until We know those who strive among you and the steadfast, and We will test your reports.﴾

The lam in His saying "la-nabluwannakum" (la-nabluwannakum) is a preparatory lam (lam al-muwatti'ah) introducing an omitted oath.

The majority of the seven readers, except Shu'bah on the authority of 'Asim, read this letter with the nun that indicates majesty (nun al-'azamah) in the three verbs: la-nabluwannakum, na'lama, and nabluwa.

Shu'bah, on the authority of 'Asim, read it with the yaʾ of the third person (al-muthannah al-tahtiyyah).

The subject pronoun refers to Allah, and to what this noble verse includes, namely that Allah, Majestic and Exalted, tests people, that is, He examines them with obligations, such as giving up lives and wealth in jihad, so that thereby the truthful among them may be distinguished from the liars, and the believer from the disbeliever. This has been made clear in other verses, such as His saying: ﴿Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while there has not yet come to you the example of those who passed away before you? Adversity and hardship touched them, and they were shaken until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the help of Allah?"﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 214].

And His saying: ﴿Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while Allah has not yet known those of you who fought and made known the steadfast?﴾ [Al 'Imran: 142].

And His saying: ﴿Or do you think you will be left alone while Allah has not yet known those of you who strove and did not take other than Allah and His Messenger and the believers as intimate associates? And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 142].

And His saying: ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim. Do the people think they will be left to say, "We believe," and they will not be tried? And We had certainly tried those before them, and Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful and will surely make evident the liars.﴾ [Al-'Ankabut: 1-3]; (the text reads al-Tawbah: 16, as in the source).

And His saying: ﴿Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in until He distinguishes the wicked from the good. And Allah would not reveal to you the unseen.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 179].

(p-385) And His saying in this noble verse: ﴿until We know those who strive﴾ [Muhammad: 31].

We have already set out the resolution of the difficulty concerning its like in Surah al-Baqarah, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿And We did not make the qiblah which you used to be on except that We might know who would follow the Messenger from who would turn back on his heels﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 143].

There we said, in that regard, the following: The apparent meaning of this verse may lead the ignorant to suppose that He, Exalted, gains through testing a knowledge He did not previously have, far exalted is He above that with great exaltation. Rather, He, Exalted, knows everything that will be before it comes to be.

He has made clear that He does not gain through testing knowledge He did not previously have, by His saying, Majestic and Exalted: ﴿And that Allah may test what is in your breasts and purify what is in your hearts. And Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 154].

So His saying: ﴿And Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾ after His saying "li-yabtaliya" is a decisive proof that He does not gain through testing anything He was not already aware of, far exalted is He above that with great exaltation, because the One Who knows what is within the breasts is free of need of testing.

In this verse there is a great clarification of all the verses in which Allah mentions His testing of His creation.

The meaning of "illa li-na'lama" is: knowledge upon which reward and punishment are based; so it does not contradict that He had knowledge of it before that. The benefit of testing is the manifestation of the matter to people. As for the Knower of the secret and the private conversation, He knows everything that will be, as is not hidden. Ended.

Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir of this noble verse the following: (This knowledge is the knowledge upon which the recompense falls, for He only rewards them for their deeds, not for His eternal knowledge of them. So its interpretation is: "until We know the strivers" with the knowledge of witnessing, for when they are commanded to act, what they do is witnessed, and the reward and punishment fall upon the knowledge of witnessing. "And We will test your reports" – We will examine them and make them manifest.) End of the relevant point.

And Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir al-Tabari said in his tafsir of this noble verse the following: (p-386) (And We will surely test you, O believers, with killing and with striving against the enemies of Allah, "until We know those of you who strive," meaning: until My party and My allies know, among you, the people of jihad in the cause of Allah and the people of patience in fighting His enemies, so that this becomes manifest to them; and those of insight in His religion are recognized among you from those with doubt and confusion about it, and the people of faith from the people of hypocrisy. "And We will test your reports," so that We may know the truthful among you from the liar.) End of the relevant point in his own wording.

What he mentioned, that the intended meaning of His saying "until We know those who strive" is: until Our party and Our allies know among you the strivers and the steadfast, has a basis, and His saying "And We will test your reports," meaning: We will make them manifest and bring them out to the people, may point to it.

And His saying: ﴿Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in until He distinguishes the wicked from the good﴾ [Al 'Imran: 179]; because the intended meaning of distinguishing the wicked from the good is that this becomes manifest to people.

For this reason He said: ﴿And Allah would not reveal to you the unseen﴾ [Al 'Imran: 179], so that you would know what the wicked and the good conceal within them. But Allah made you aware of that through testing and trial, by which the inner states of people, of wickedness and goodness, become apparent.

The first opinion is also sound, and knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 47, verse 32:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [others] from the way of Allah and oppose the Messenger after guidance has become clear to them will never harm Allah at all, and He will make their deeds fruitless.﴾ The apparent meaning is that "ṣaddū" (averted [others]) in this verse is transitive, and its object is omitted, i.e., they disbelieved and averted others from the way of Allah, so they are astray and lead others astray.

We have already noted in the commentary on surah al-Nahl, in discussing His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely reward them for the best of what they used to do﴾ [al-Nahl: 97], that ta'sīs (establishing a new meaning) takes precedence over ta'kīd (emphasis), as is established in the principles of jurisprudence (uṣūl).

If "ṣaddū" here is taken as intransitive, then the meaning of ṣudūd is disbelief, and it serves as ta'kīd (emphasis) for His saying: "disbelieved."

If it is taken as transitive, then it is ta'sīs (establishing a new meaning), because His saying "disbelieved" indicates their disbelief within themselves.

His saying "and averted [others]," taken as transitive, indicates that they compelled others to disbelief and turned them away from the truth, and this is more probable than what precedes it.

His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿and opposed the Messenger﴾ means they opposed Muhammad (ﷺ) with severe opposition.

This noble verse indicates two matters. The first is that those who disbelieve and avert others from the truth and oppose him (ﷺ) will never harm Allah by their disbelief at all, because He is free of need in Himself, with absolute independence.

The second is that they only harm themselves by this, because that disbelief is the cause of the nullification of their deeds, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿and He will make their deeds fruitless.﴾

These two matters contained in this noble verse have been clarified in verses of the Book of Allah.

Among the verses indicating the first, which is Allah's independence from His creation and that He is not harmed by their disobedience, is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whoever disbelieves - indeed, Allah is free of need from the worlds﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 97].

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿If you disbelieve, indeed Allah is free of need from you﴾ [al-Zumar: 7].

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Moses said: If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on earth entirely, indeed Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy﴾ [Ibrāhīm: 8].

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They say, "Allah has taken a son." Exalted is He; He is the Free of need. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ [Yūnus: 68].

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So they disbelieved and turned away, and Allah was Free of need, and Allah is Praiseworthy﴾ [al-Taghābun: 6].

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O mankind, you are the poor toward Allah, and Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy﴾ [Fāṭir: 15], among other verses.

Among the verses indicating the second, which is the nullification of their deeds by disbelief, that is, their invalidation by it, is His saying (p-388) may He be exalted: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust﴾ [al-Furqān: 23].

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The example of those who disbelieve in their Lord is that their deeds are like ashes which the wind blows on a stormy day﴾ [Ibrāhīm: 18].

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who disbelieve - their deeds are like a mirage in a level plain, which the thirsty one thinks is water until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing﴾ [al-Nūr: 39].

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter except the Fire, and what they did therein has become worthless, and what they used to do is void﴾ [Hūd: 16], among other verses.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 47, verse 33:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger﴾.

We have already presented a great many verses similar to this one shortly before, in the course of our lengthy discussion on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then do they not reflect upon the Qur'an?﴾ (an-Nisa' 4:82) and what follows it [47/24].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 47, verse 34:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [others] from the way of Allah and then die while they are disbelievers – never will Allah forgive them﴾.

What this noble verse contains, that whoever dies upholding disbelief, Allah will not forgive him, because the Fire became obligatory for him by his death upon disbelief, has been made clear in other verses of the Book of Allah, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers – never will be accepted from any of them the earth filled with gold even if he sought to ransom himself by it. Those will have a painful punishment, and they will have no helpers﴾ [Surat Ali 'Imran: 91].

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers – upon them is the curse of Allah and of the angels and of mankind, all together. Abiding eternally therein; the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved﴾ [al-Baqarah: 161–162].

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who die while they are disbelievers – for them We have prepared a painful punishment﴾ [an-Nisa': 18].

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever of you reverts from his religion and dies while he is a disbeliever – those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter, and those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally﴾ [al-Baqarah: 217].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 47, verse 35:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So do not weaken and call to peace while you are the superior, and Allah is with you and will not deprive you of your deeds.﴾ (p-389) The majority of the Seven Readers, except Hamzah and Shu'bah from 'Asim, read this word ﴿ilā as-salm﴾ with a fatḥah on the sīn.

Hamzah and Shu'bah read "ilā as-silm" with a kasrah on the sīn.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So do not weaken﴾ means do not become feeble and humiliated. From it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they did not weaken for what afflicted them in the way of Allah﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 146].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is so, and [know] that Allah weakens the plot of the disbelievers﴾ [al-Anfāl: 18], meaning He makes their plot feeble. And the saying of Zuhayr ibn Abī Sulmā:

"The daughter of al-Bakrī broke her promise to you, so the rope became weak and worn out from her."

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿while you are the superior﴾ is a circumstantial clause (jumlah ḥāliyyah), meaning: do not become feeble in fighting the disbelievers, ﴿and call to peace﴾, meaning do not begin by seeking peace, that is, reconciliation and truce, ﴿while you are the superior﴾, meaning while the state is that you are the superior, that is, the ones who prevail over and overcome your enemies, and because you hope from Allah for victory and reward what they do not hope for.

This interpretation of His saying ﴿while you are the superior﴾ is the correct one.

It is supported by verses of the Book of Allah, such as His saying after it ﴿and Allah is with you﴾, because whoever Allah is with is the superior, the victorious, the dominant, the one granted victory and promised reward; so he is worthy of not weakening in confronting the disbelievers and of not beginning with them by seeking reconciliation and truce.

Such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed Our army will be the victors﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 173],

and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed We will surely help Our messengers and those who believe in the life of this world﴾ [Ghāfir: 51],

and His saying: ﴿And it was upon Us to help the believers﴾ [al-Rūm: 47],

and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands and disgrace them and give you victory over them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 14].

Among what clarifies the meaning of this verse on fighting is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not weaken in pursuit of the people. If you are suffering, they are suffering as you suffer, but you hope from Allah for what they do not hope﴾ [al-Nisā': 104]; because His saying, exalted is He: ﴿but you hope from Allah for what they do not hope﴾ refers to the victory which Allah has promised you, and dominance and abundant reward.

(p-390) This is like His saying here: ﴿while you are the superior﴾ and His saying: ﴿and Allah is with you﴾, meaning with victory, support and reward.

Know that this verse on fighting has no contradiction with the verse of al-Anfāl so that it could be said that one of them abrogates the other (naskh); rather both are muḥkam (established), and each one is revealed in a situation different from the situation in which the other was revealed.

So the prohibition in this verse on fighting, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So do not weaken and call to peace﴾, is only about initiating the seeking of peace.

The command to incline to peace in the verse of al-Anfāl applies when the disbelievers initiate seeking peace and inclining toward it, as is clear in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if they incline to peace, then incline to it, and put your trust in Allah﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Anfāl: 61].

As for His saying in this noble verse: ﴿and Allah is with you﴾, we have already presented the verses clarifying it at the end of Surat al-Naḥl, in discussing His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good﴾ [al-Naḥl: 128]. What we have mentioned about the meaning of this verse is more preferable and more correct than what Ibn Kathīr (may Allah have mercy on him) explained it with.

Namely, the meaning is: do not call to reconciliation and truce while you are the superior, that is, in the state of your strength and ability to wage jihad. And if you are in weakness and lack of strength, then there is no obstacle to your calling to peace, that is, reconciliation and truce. From it is the saying of al-ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās al-Sulamī:

"Peace takes from them what you are pleased with, and war suffices you from its breaths, which are sips."

His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿and He will not deprive you of your deeds﴾, meaning He will not diminish for you anything of the reward of your deeds.

This meaning contained in this noble verse, that He, exalted is He, diminishes nothing of the reward of deeds, is made clear in other verses, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if you obey Allah and His Messenger, He will not deprive you of anything of your deeds﴾ [al-Ḥujurāt: 14], meaning He will not diminish anything of their reward.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged in the least. And even if it is the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth. And sufficient are We as reckoners﴾ [al-Anbiyā': 47].

(p-391) Verses of this kind are many and well known, and we have presented them repeatedly.

His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿and He will not deprive you (yatiraku-kum)﴾, its origin is from al-watr, which is the single (fard).

So the root of His saying "lan yitirakum" is: He will not single you out and strip you of your deeds, rather He will pay them in full to you.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 47, verse 36:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if you believe and fear God, He will give you your rewards﴾.

These rewards which God promised to those who believe and fear Him are made clear in many verses, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who believe, fear God and believe in His Messenger; He will give you a double portion of His mercy, and will appoint for you a light by which you will walk, and will forgive you. And God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Hadid: 28], and other verses besides this.

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And He will not ask you for your wealth﴾. In this noble verse there are well-known views among the people of tafsir (tafsir, the science of Qur'anic exegesis). Among them is that the meaning is: the Prophet (ﷺ) will not ask you for your wealth as a reward for what he has conveyed to you of the revelation, which contains the good of this world and the Hereafter.

This view is supported by many verses of the Book of God, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Whatever reward I have asked of you, it is yours. My reward is only with God﴾ [Saba: 47].

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it, and I am not of those who pretend﴾ [Sad: 86].

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or do you ask them for a reward, so that they are burdened with debt?﴾ [al-Tur: 40].

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah Hud, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And O my people, I do not ask you for wealth for it; my reward is only with God﴾ [Hud: 29], and we mentioned some of that in Surah al-Shura, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: I do not ask you for any reward for it, except affection among kin﴾ [al-Shura: 23].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 47, verse 38:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah is the Self-Sufficient, and you are the needy﴾. We have already presented the verses that clarify this earlier, in our discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [others] from the way of Allah and oppose the Messenger after guidance has been made clear to them...﴾ [Muhammad: 32], to the end of the verse.
